features.name: selector variables, filters, ranges, position/delta, rotation, sort, limit, names, teams, tags, scores, advancements, NBT, and predicates

features.name: execute chain context changes, redirects/forks, as/at/in/positioned/rotated/align/anchored/facing/on/summon, if/unless conditions, run, and store result/success
features.reason: The execute store gap is confirmed by a whole-repository/current-caller search, not by the absence of one registration snippet alone. Official ExecuteCommand::register adds literal store with result and success, and wrapStores supplies score, bossbar and data target branches; official storeValue/storeData attach a CommandResultCallback through CommandSourceStack.withCallback. Current execute.rs::register has run/as/at/in/positioned/rotated/align/anchored/facing/summon/on/if/unless branches and redirects back to the execute node, but no literal("store") branch. Exact current git grep for literal("store"), executeStore, wrapStores, storeValue and storeData returned no implementation match in Pumpkin/codegen command sources; the only targeted broad store hits were comments describing stored command context. ResultValueTaker, CommandSource::call_result and dispatcher on_command_completion are generic result propagation seams, not a parser/target/mutation implementation for execute store.
features.expected: The execute tree can mutate source context, fork over selected entities, test conditions, store command result/success into score/NBT targets, and redirect into the root command chain.
features.current: Pumpkin registers most context changes, on-relations, if/unless entity/block/loaded/dimension/biome/blocks/score/data, and run redirects. The registration has no store literal and no result/success store branch; the shared ResultValueTaker exists but is not the official execute store tree contract.
features.impact: A command string such as /execute store result score <target> <objective> run ... or the bossbar/data variants cannot parse through the current execute tree. The generic callback can report a command result to existing consumers, but it does not create score/NBT/bossbar storage targets or the required scaling branches.
features.first_repro: execute.rs register + whole-caller grep -> zero store literal; official register -> store/result/success

limits.limitations: No command parse or execution was run.

features.name: AND/OR/inverted, entity/block/tool/NBT, damage/location/weather/time/score, and predicate references
features.reason: The small generated LootCondition enum is not, by itself, evidence that all loot support is absent or that runtime datapack handling follows the same route. Current source has a real compile-time loot projection and a shared evaluator used by block, entity, chest/minecart/trial and /loot paths. The precise gap is lossy condition projection: parse_condition recognizes survives_explosion, killed_by_player, random/enchantment/table bonus, all_of and only shears/silk heuristics for match_tool/any_of/inverted; unrecognized official conditions become LootCondition::None, and check_condition treats None as true. Official LootItemConditions::bootstrap/LootItemCondition/LootContext provide registry-backed, context-rich evaluation for entity, block-state, tool/NBT, damage, location, weather, time, score, reference and related conditions. The separate runtime datapack loader currently loads recipes/functions/function-tags/test instances, not runtime loot tables, but that is a separate reload/resource boundary and is not used as the sole basis for this row. Client pack metadata was also separated: official PackMetadataSection.CLIENT_TYPE is applied when a client resource pack is read, SERVER_TYPE when server data packs are read; current resource-pack push only sends configured URL/hash/prompt/force, while read_pack_mcmeta is used for server datapack description/format/known-pack listing and feature/known-pack publication. Neither path converts client metadata into loot conditions.
features.expected: Decode and evaluate the official registry-backed condition set against the complete LootContext, including named predicate resources and NBT/component-aware tool/entity checks.
features.current: Only a small enum and lossy parser exist: survives_explosion, killed_by_player, random, enchanted bonus, table bonus, all_of, and shears/silk heuristics. any_of/inverted only cover special silk/shears cases; entity, block state, NBT, damage source, location, weather, time, score, and predicate references are not evaluated.
features.impact: Built-in generated loot can become unconditional or partial when a restrictive condition is reduced to None; natural drops and command/chest consumers can therefore differ for the measured condition classes. features.name: DamageSource tag gates and hurtServer/actuallyHurt cooldown ordering
features.reason: The broad claim that damage tags are generally incomplete is withdrawn. Current Pumpkin does use concrete tag conditions for BYPASSES_ARMOR, BYPASSES_EFFECTS, BYPASSES_RESISTANCE, BYPASSES_ENCHANTMENTS, and BYPASSES_SHIELD. The official 26.2 BYPASSES_INVULNERABILITY resource contains exactly out_of_world and generic_kill, and current Entity::is_invulnerable_to hard-codes that same pair; this is not reported as a built-in BYPASSES_INVULNERABILITY mismatch. The confirmed difference is the separate hurt/invulnerability-tick cooldown contract: official LivingEntity::hurtServer checks DamageTypeTags.BYPASSES_COOLDOWN and compares the post-blocking amount, while current LivingEntity::damage_with_context hard-codes only generic_kill/out_of_world and stores the pre-armor/pre-magic amount in last_damage_taken. General invulnerable state and damage_immunities are entity-state immunity gates, not tag bypasses and not hurt ticks.
features.expected: The server rejects invulnerable/dead targets first, applies fire/effect and tag-specific gates, blocking, freeze/helmet handling, and then uses the post-blocking damage for the 20-tick hurt cooldown. BYPASSES_COOLDOWN and BYPASSES_INVULNERABILITY are tag contracts, not a hard-coded two-type exception.
features.current: Pumpkin has the generated 26.2 tag sets and checks bypass armor/effects/resistance/enchantments for reductions, but Entity::is_invulnerable_to exempts only GENERIC_KILL and OUT_OF_WORLD. LivingEntity stores the original pre-armor/magic amount in last_damage_taken and bypasses hurt cooldown only for those same two types; no BYPASSES_COOLDOWN tag is consulted.
features.impact: For an existing central damage caller where armor, effects, or blocking change the amount, a second hit inside the hurt window can be accepted/rejected using a different last-damage baseline than official. A future/current damage type covered by BYPASSES_COOLDOWN is not generically honored by Pumpkin. By contrast, BYPASSES_INVULNERABILITY is not claimed missing for the two official built-ins; custom Entity::damage_immunities and the general invulnerable flag remain separate gates, and no current gameplay caller to set_damage_immunity was found.
actual_source: current all-callers grep: damage_with_context in 45 source occurrences across 24 files
features.first_repro: Static differential fixture: apply two damages within the 20-tick hurt window to an entity with armor/resistance or a blocking reduction. Official stores/comparisons use the post-blocking damage value; current last_damage_taken stores the amount before armor/magic reduction. Separate tag fixture: inject or otherwise construct a damage type with BYPASSES_COOLDOWN and compare the second-hit gate; no current dynamic custom-tag runtime path is established. Neither fixture was executed.

features.name: player/vehicle finite-value validation, NaN/Infinity handling, and coordinate bounds
features.final_verdict_raw: qualified difference: the position-only Infinity/rejection subclaim is retracted; the vehicle validation/clamp gap remains confirmed
features.reason: The official 26.2 containsInvalidValues bytecode calls Double.isNaN for x/y/z, not Double.isFinite, and calls Floats.isFinite only for the two float rotations. Therefore an Infinity coordinate in handleMovePlayer is not rejected by that helper; handleMovePlayer then applies clampHorizontal/clampVertical. Pumpkin handle_position also tests only is_nan and then applies the same numeric bounds, so the claimed official-position-Infinity-versus-Pumpkin-is_nan difference is not a valid defect. The surviving difference is the vehicle path: official handleMoveVehicle applies containsInvalidValues, clamps x/y/z, and wraps rotations before authority/movement handling; Pumpkin handle_move_vehicle performs no finite/NaN gate or coordinate clamp and writes packet coordinates/rotations directly to the vehicle and player. Position+rotation being stricter about infinite coordinates is an inverse behavior difference, not evidence of an Infinity bypass.
features.expected: 26.2 rejects NaN/invalid rotation values, clamps horizontal coordinates to [-3.0E7, 3.0E7] and vertical coordinates to [-2.0E7, 2.0E7], and applies the same invalid-value gate to vehicle movement before authority checks.
features.current: Position-only movement checks x/y/z with is_nan, so Infinity is not rejected before clamp. Position+rotation and rotation-only paths use is_finite for coordinates/angles. handle_move_vehicle performs no finite-value validation and writes packet coordinates/rotation directly.
features.impact: The retained P1 condition requires a vehicle packet reaching JavaClient::handle_move_vehicle while a vehicle is present or while the handler still writes the player transform: the packet contains NaN/Infinity, or a finite coordinate outside the official horizontal/vertical bounds, and the current path is not stopped by another caller-side guard. The position-only player packet Infinity case is not an impact condition because both paths clamp it after a NaN-only coordinate gate.
features.first_repro: Static input A: SPlayerPosition with x=+Infinity. Official containsInvalidValues returns false for the coordinate portion, handleMovePlayer clamps x to 3.0E7; Pumpkin handle_position's is_nan checks pass and clamp_horizontal also yields 3.0E7. Static input B: SMoveVehicle with x=+Infinity or x=4.0E7. Official handleMoveVehicle gates/clamps before authority checks; Pumpkin handle_move_vehicle constructs Vector3(packet.x, ...) and calls set_pos without either guard. No packet was injected.

limits.limitations: No packet fixture or runtime kick/correction observation; the official double check is NaN-only while float rotation uses finite, as shown by javap.

features.name: movement/collision behavior at unloaded chunks and chunk ticket/update ordering
features.reason: Current and official 26.2 call paths were compared for the named condition. Current: World::get_block_state_id_if_loaded returns None for an unloaded chunk, and get_block_state falls back to AIR. get_block_collisions therefore sees no block collision in an unloaded area. Packet movement stores the target position first and calls chunker::update_position afterward, so chunk ticket/update ordering cannot protect the initial acceptance. Expected: Official collision queries use collision chunks/level access, and the server chunk source moves/tickets the player as part of the authoritative movement flow; unloaded collision data is not silently treated as an empty world for accepted movement.

features.name: food, XP, score/statistics, advancements, effects, inventory and ender chest persistence across reconnect/respawn
features.reason: Current and official 26.2 call paths were compared for the named condition. Current: Pumpkin writes/reads food, XP, score, stats, inventory, ender chest, effects, abilities and respawn state in player NBT; advancements load from a separate JSON file and save on disconnect/shutdown. Expected: FoodData, XP level/progress/total, score/statistics, inventory/ender chest, abilities/effects and advancement progress survive a reconnect with the same UUID; save ownership and load ownership are explicit and consistent.

features.name: playerdata load, periodic autosave, logout save, compressed NBT replacement, corruption fallback, and data-version migration
features.reason: Current and official 26.2 call paths were compared for the named condition. Current: Pumpkin periodically snapshots online Player NBT and saves it on a rayon task; logout calls player.remove first and then handle_player_leave. PlayerDataStorage::save_player_data uses File::create directly on the final UUID.dat path, with no temp/safe-replace, backup, or data-fixer step. Load errors are logged and converted to default/no-data by ServerPlayerData::load_data, so corrupt data can silently become a new default state. DATA_VERSION is written, but no official PLAYER datafix migration is applied. Expected: Official playerdata save serializes current player state with a data version, writes a temporary compressed file, safely replaces the UUID .dat, keeps a backup path, and load applies the PLAYER data fixer before returning; logout invokes PlayerList save before removal cleanup.

features.name: disconnect menu closure, vehicles/riders, projectile cleanup, chunk tickets, entity tracker removal, player info and leave events

features.name: normal reconnect state restoration, duplicate-login exclusion, UUID ownership, stale connection cleanup, and listing consistency
features.reason: Current and official 26.2 call paths were compared for the named condition. Current: Normal reconnect loads UUID.dat and publishes a new Player. Duplicate login is not rejected or disconnected: PlayerMembership is an append-only Arc vector, World::get_player_by_uuid returns the first matching entry, and Server::retire_duplicate_chat_owners only retires the old chat capability. Later removal contains replacement-preserving tracker/listing logic, but two same-UUID live Player objects can coexist until cleanup. Expected: A normal reconnect with the same UUID loads the prior state, while a duplicate login disconnects the existing profile owner and leaves one authoritative UUID entry; stale disconnect cleanup must not remove the replacement or corrupt listing/tracking state.

features.name: spectator camera target, camera reset, spectator visibility, entity tracking pairing, and tracking cleanup
features.reason: Current and official 26.2 call paths were compared for the named condition. Current: Pumpkin stores camera_target_id, follows a target's position during Player::tick when the target is found in the current world, resets to self when missing, and has spectator-aware generic tracker predicates. Current: Pumpkin has BreedGoal, love ticks, breeder UUID, cooldown decrement/storage, advancement/stat/XP/event paths, and creates offspring through from_type followed by age=-24000. features.name: entity NBT spawn initialization, spawn reason, variant inheritance/defaults, and RNG
features.reason: Current and official 26.2 call paths were compared for the named condition. Current: from_type builds a Rust entity with defaults or constructor RNG; natural, base-spawner, trial, raid, and dragon paths mostly call from_type plus rotation and direct spawn. Trial reads only selected IsBaby/Size/equipment fields; structure entities are the main path that reads full NBT after construction. No common spawn-reason/finalizeSpawn pipeline was found, and variant-bearing constructors such as chicken/fox/frog/horse/llama use independent defaults/random values. Expected: Each spawn reason loads entity NBT through the official processor, applies position/rotation, difficulty and spawn-reason finalization, equipment/custom rules, passenger recursion, entity-specific variant RNG/inheritance, and only then inserts the entity.
features.expected: Each spawn reason loads entity NBT through the official processor, applies position/rotation, difficulty and spawn-reason finalization, equipment/custom rules, passenger recursion, entity-specific variant RNG/inheritance, and only then inserts the entity.

Current: Pumpkin stores passenger and vehicle links, broadcasts CSetPassengers, applies a 60-tick riding cooldown, and searches block-safe dismount positions with standing/crouching/swimming dimensions. add_passenger itself does not reject an existing vehicle, duplicate passenger, cycle, or cross-world link, and no shared root/control validation path was found. features.name: pending/live promotion, source of truth, migration, removal, and chunk unload ownership
features.reason: The ownership difference is real: official LevelChunk removes a pending tag before promotion and uses live-or-packed fallback for saving. Pumpkin get_block_entity checks live first but reads pending with get() and retains that shadow; migrate_pending_block_entities then calls update_block_entity, and explicit save_block_entities rewrites the shadow from the live object. features.name: full NBT mutation, live object update, command data path, and WASM set/get path
features.reason: The full-NBT mutation root is real for an already-live block entity. Official BlockDataAccessor::setData calls BlockEntity::loadWithComponents on the live object, then setChanged and Level::sendBlockUpdated. Current BlockDataAccessor::set_data and the WASM set_block_entity_nbt caller only call World::add_block_entity_nbt, which writes the pending NBT map and marks the chunk dirty. World::get_block_entity returns the live map first, so the existing live object is not reloaded from that pending tag. The pending-only alternate path does exist: get_block_entity can parse pending NBT into a live object, and migrate_pending_block_entities calls get_block_entity then update_block_entity when the position is not already loaded. That helper does not repair the already-live mutation path, and it leaves the pending shadow in place.
features.expected: BlockDataAccessor.setData loads the supplied compound into the already-live BlockEntity through loadWithComponents, calls setChanged, and sends a block update. getData returns saveWithFullMetadata. A mutation must affect the live object immediately and persist with later saves.
features.current: The command BlockDataAccessor::set_data only inserts the supplied tag into pending_block_entities. The WASM set_block_entity_nbt path likewise parses bytes, overwrites x/y/z, and inserts pending NBT. get_block_entity returns an existing live map entry before consulting pending, so an already-live entity does not consume the mutation; a later save_block_entities can overwrite the pending mutation with old live state.
features.impact: For a live furnace/chest/sign/etc., /data block mutation or the WASM API can leave reads and the live ticker on the old typed state. A later explicit World::save, shutdown, or chunk-eviction snapshot serializes that old live state back into pending storage, so the requested NBT can be overwritten. This is a concrete stale-state/save path, not a claim that every fresh pending-only entity is lost.
features.first_repro: Static path: live BlockEntity at P -> BlockDataAccessor::set_data(P, changed NBT) or WASM set_block_entity_nbt(P, NBT) -> pending_block_entities[P] changes while block_entities[P] remains old -> get_data reads old live state -> World::save -> save_block_entities -> old write_internal output replaces pending NBT. The pending-only path is separate: get_block_entity(P) parses pending NBT and migrate_pending_block_entities(P) calls update_block_entity; no runtime execution.

limits.limitations: No command, WASM, packet, storage, restart, or runtime live-object assertion was executed.
limits.impact_conditions: An already-live block entity is targeted by /data merge/modify block or the WASM set_block_entity_nbt API, the supplied NBT changes a typed field, and a later live snapshot occurs before a separate promotion of the pending tag. For a pending-only entity, get_block_entity may promote it first; that branch is not the stale-live case. No P0 is assigned for speculative fresh-factory or viewer effects.

features.name: tick eligibility, migration timing, unload/shutdown save, autosave, and reload boundary
features.reason: The save boundary difference is concrete. World::save, World::shutdown, and remove_entities_in_chunks explicitly call save_block_entities before the chunk/live map is released. In contrast, pumpkin-world GenerationSchedule::save_all_chunk selects dirty Level chunks, clones ChunkData, and sends it to IO without a World::save_block_entities call. ChunkData serializes pending_block_entities only. Therefore direct chunk autosave can persist an older pending snapshot when a live BE changed and the chunk is dirty for any independent reason. This review does not relabel the existing explicit save routes as missing or data-loss fixes as broken.
features.expected: Only ticking/full-status block entities tick; post-load promotion registers them and consumes pending tags. Saving asks each live entity for full metadata, while unload/removal and reload preserve the current state exactly.
features.current: World::tick snapshots live block entities in active chunks and ticks them in parallel. Migration only promotes entries when chunks become active and leaves pending shadows. Explicit World::save, World::shutdown, and chunk eviction call save_block_entities, but the chunk-system autosave path save_all_chunk serializes ChunkData directly and has no call to save live block entities first.
features.impact: A live BE has changed; its pending snapshot is stale; and the direct chunk-system save_all_chunk path runs while that Level chunk is dirty. The path is especially concrete when another block/chunk operation marks the chunk dirty. Real restart loss was not executed.
features.first_repro: Live chest inventory changes -> BE dirty flag is set but pending NBT is unchanged -> another block operation makes ChunkData dirty -> GenerationSchedule::save_all_chunk clones/writes ChunkData directly -> internal_to_bytes emits pending_block_entities, not live map serialization. Static only.

limits.limitations: No IO write, restart, reload, or hash comparison was executed; no P0 because the concrete storage outcome remains unexecuted.

features.name: container inventory semantics, furnace progress/fuel/recipe state, chest viewers/loot, and ticker side effects
features.reason: Slots, furnace progress, lit state, recipe-use accounting, chest loot fields, and a custom viewer tracker are present. The official contracts are broader: furnace uses registry RecipeManager/FuelValues and exact side effects; chest uses ContainerOpenersCounter, recheckOpeners, lid controller, block events, and game-event/menu integration. Pumpkin's custom ViewerCountTracker is evidence of an existing viewer path, so the finding is not 'old viewers are lost' and is not P0. The remaining local-vs-official semantics are static and subset-scoped.
features.expected: Furnaces persist three inventory slots, cooking/lit timers, recipe-use counts, and use registry recipe checks and FuelValues while updating LIT state. Chests persist items or deferred loot tables and use ContainerOpenersCounter/lid/block events for viewer state.
features.current: Pumpkin persists furnace slots, snake_case progress/lit fields, and RecipesUsed; it ticks a local recipe/fuel implementation and updates the lit block state. Chest-like entities persist slots and deferred loot fields and use a custom ViewerCountTracker, but do not have the official openers-counter/ticker/menu side-effect implementation. Static data coverage is substantial but not end-to-end equivalent.

features.name: jukebox record, song/player state, tick progression, redstone/comparator state, and reload
features.reason: The reload arc is concretely incomplete. Official JukeboxBlockEntity.loadAdditional restores the record and, when ticks_since_song_started is present, sets the song player from the record-derived JukeboxSong; the ticker then delegates to that player. Pumpkin from_nbt restores ticks_since_song_started but initializes song_length_ticks to zero, so tick/is_playing cannot resume a loaded song. Existing set_record/start_playing and comparator/dirty paths are not missing claims; they do not repair the reload state.
features.expected: The official JukeboxSongPlayer derives the song from the playable record component, plays/stops on item changes, persists ticks_since_song_started, resumes the song player on load, ticks it every tick, updates HAS_RECORD/neighbours/game events, and exposes the song comparator output.
features.current: Pumpkin stores RecordItem and ticks_since_song_started, but from_nbt resets song_length_ticks to 0. The world tick therefore cannot continue a loaded song; the placement path manually calls start_playing and emits the play event, while set_record itself only marks dirty. Stop/play/game-event and comparator behavior is split across custom block code.

features.name: player advancement JSON persistence, join load, reload tree replacement and listener cleanup
features.reason: The raw confirmed-difference conclusion was too strong because PlayerAdvancement::new is not the only construction path. Current production startup/login flow is explicit: Server::add_player calls ServerPlayerData::load_data(profile.id), constructs Player::new, then after wrapping the player in Arc locks player.advancements and calls PlayerAdvancement::load(); the loaded advancement file is under AdvancementManager::advancement_path/{uuid}.json. Save paths exist in AdvancementManager::save_all_players/save_player and Server::save_all. The remaining static differences are real but narrower: PlayerAdvancement::reload clears local progress/visibility state and calls load, but its stopListening call is a TODO; Pumpkin has no CriteriaTriggers/CriterionTrigger listener registry, no active listener registration/unregistration and no official dynamic ServerAdvancementManager/datafix codec path. No production caller for reload was found in the current source search, so reload publication/cleanup reachability is unconfirmed rather than treated as a missing join load.
features.expected: PlayerAdvancements loads the per-player file during construction, applies datafix/codec data against the current advancement manager, checks automatic triggers, registers listeners, and reload clears old triggers/tree/progress before loading the replacement.
features.current: PlayerAdvancement::load and reload exist, but new player construction only creates the object; no join/spawn call to `load` was found. `reload` has a commented `stopListening` TODO and only clears local maps. The manager uses static generated Advancement values rather than a runtime ServerAdvancementManager/datafix codec.
features.impact: Reconnect/load persistence is present on the shown production path, so the raw claim that a reconnect starts with empty advancement progress is retracted. Remaining impact is limited to datapack/tree reload and trigger semantics: no official listener registry or trigger cleanup exists, static generated advancement definitions are used, and reload behavior is not shown to be invoked or to replace a live dynamic tree with official listener cleanup.
features.first_repro: Server::add_player -> load_data -> Player::new -> advancements.load; reload has TODO listener cleanup

features.name: item consume event boundary, cooldown, spectator/feature gates, rotation, and creative item preservation
features.reason: official contractとcurrent static pathの差/部分実装は残るが、runtime結果・data-loss・security exploitまで未確認。generic helper/default component/trait fallthroughを専用関数不在の根拠にしていない。
features.expected: Use-item packets reject empty/disabled items, acknowledge sequence, respect spectator/cooldown, use the packet rotation, and preserve the count in infinite/creative mode. Consume-specific events must be tied to actual consumption, not every item-use packet.
features.current: Pumpkin fires PlayerItemConsumeEvent for every SUseItem before item behavior and before the registry cooldown check, and cancellation returns for any item including non-consumables. features.expected: Official patterns are validated, trimmed to the non-empty bounding rectangle, require exact ingredient count and dimensions, reject extra occupied cells, and try mirrored matching only for non-symmetrical patterns.

features.name: shapeless ingredient multiplicity and multiset matching
features.reason: shapelessの重複ingredientは使用済みスロット集合でmultiset相当の照合を行う。recipe result/remainder/componentの別問題をこの行のingredient multiplicityへ混ぜない。
features.expected: The number of occupied input slots equals the ingredient list size, and duplicate ingredients are consumed as a multiset rather than as a set; each occupied slot is matched against one distinct ingredient.
features.current: Current static and dynamic shapeless matching requires count == ingredients.len(), tracks a used boolean per ingredient, and rejects an unmatched occupied slot. Duplicate simple/tag ingredients therefore have a distinct-slot path comparable to the official multiplicity rule.
features.impact: Basic duplicate-item recipes are structurally covered, but dynamic ingredient alternatives are less complete and result/stack-component semantics are not covered by this matcher; this must not be generalized to full shapeless equivalence.
features.first_repro: Static matrix: two identical ingredients, two alternative ingredients, one extra occupied slot, and one missing occupied slot. Current boolean assignment handles the first matrix, while parser/codec omissions remain outside it.

features.name: use-max placement, batching, per-slot consumption, and output/item-max conservation
features.reason: The old P0 wording is narrowed. compute_biggest_craftable has a 64 upper bound and aggregates by item ID/count, but does not read ItemStack max-stack components. handle_place_recipe then calls take_n_ingredient, which combines matching inventory stacks into one ItemStack, and writes it directly with CraftingInventory::set_stack; this bypasses NormalSlot::can_insert and slot max validation during recipe placement. Therefore a max-one/component-limited ingredient can be placed over its effective stack limit in the crafting grid when multiple inventory stacks are aggregated. This is a concrete placement difference, not proof of a runtime duplication exploit.
features.expected: use_max uses stacked ingredient accounting, reuses the current grid amount when appropriate, clamps by output/item max stack components, and places amounts through placement metadata without overstacking or losing partial inputs.
features.current: compute_biggest_craftable caps every recipe at 64 and groups inventory only by item ID; it ignores item/component max-stack values. take_n_ingredient combines matching stacks into one result stack. Existing result quick-move refills the complete output after partial insertion, so partial destination capacity can decouple taken output from ingredient consumption.
features.impact: Use-max can create an overstacked input stack in the grid for an item/component whose max is below the aggregated count. Before placement, current code always clears the grid and PlayerInventory::offer returns items to inventory or drops them when full; there is no official testClearGrid-style capacity guard. During result quick-move, ScreenHandler::insert_item does enforce destination slot/item max, so the later output move is bounded. For an accepted partial output, current code consumes one item from each input slot, refills the result, and explicitly drops the unaccepted local remainder; the static path does not establish duplication. Fragmented destination-capacity behavior across repeated quick-move iterations is not runtime-proven.
features.first_repro: Static fixture: give the player two separate stacks of an ingredient with an effective max stack of 1, send SPlaceRecipe(use_max=true) for a recipe needing that ingredient once, and inspect the grid after handle_place_recipe. Expected official path clamps/places through placement metadata; current path computes amount 2, take_n_ingredient combines the two stacks, and CraftingInventory::set_stack stores count 2. Separate capacity fixture: fill destination slots so only part of one result fits, then observe accepted output, returned/dropped remainder, repeated quick-move calls, and one-craft ingredient consumption; not executed.

features.current: IDs are synthesized from built-in crafting/cooking counts plus dynamic vector order. CRecipeBookAdd's total includes all dynamic recipes, but its writer skips DynamicRecipe::Brewing, so a dynamic brewing recipe makes the declared entry count exceed encoded entries. features.name: DataComponentPatch removal marker, default override, duplicate-key, and prototype sanitization semantics
features.reason: official contractとcurrent static pathの差/部分実装は残るが、runtime結果・data-loss・security exploitまで未確認。generic helper/default component/trait fallthroughを専用関数不在の根拠にしていない。
features.expected: Official patch keys use a removed marker, values are typed component codecs, a patch is applied over the item prototype, and sanitized patches omit a set value equal to the prototype or a removal where no prototype exists. The map is keyed uniquely by component type.
features.current: Pumpkin represents a patch as Vec<(DataComponent, Option<Box<...>>)> and writes removals as !component with an empty compound. Lookup gives the first matching patch entry, setters update only the first match, and network/NBT writers count and emit every duplicate entry. Explicit values equal to item.components remain in the patch; remove_data_component always records None even when no prototype exists. set_damage(0) removes the patch entry rather than modeling an explicit removal.
features.impact: Default overrides and repeated component entries can produce different equality, patch size, wire output, and reload behavior from vanilla. Removal of a prototype component works in the normal path, but patch canonicality is not preserved.
features.first_repro: Static input: an item whose prototype has ItemName, then set_data_component(ItemNameImpl equal to the prototype) or supply duplicate component entries. Official fromPatch sanitizes equal values; Pumpkin retains the entry and first-match lookup wins.

features.name: Long/float numeric conversion, NaN/infinity handling, signed zero, and component scalar codecs
features.reason: numeric coercionの一部差は静的に見えるが、DFU Number/各official codecを全fieldで比較していない。NaN/infinity/signed-zeroを一律gapとしない。
features.expected: DFU NbtOps exposes all NBT numeric tags through Number and primitive codecs perform the official numeric conversion/range behavior. Java floating equality/hash semantics preserve signed-zero distinctions and canonicalize NaN where the component value uses Float/Double.
features.current: Most scalar readers require the exact NBT tag type: MaxDamage/Damage/MapId require Int and float fields require Float. Some recent effect paths explicitly accept Byte/Short/Int/Long/Float/Double, while nbt_long uses Rust casts. MapDecorations accepts all numeric tags, but component equality uses Rust f32/f64 equality and its canonical hash collapses +0/-0 and NaN bits. features.name: Copy, effective component equality, canonicality, hash calculation, and actual hash caller
features.reason: zero hashを全componentの欠陥とはしないが、OptionalItemStackHashからTrackedStack::is_in_syncへ到達するcaller evidenceがあるため、effective-map/hashの差は実際の同期境界として残る。runtime hash traceは未実行。
features.expected: Official copy preserves the effective component map, equality compares item plus effective components, and hashItemAndComponents hashes item plus the full component map. Prototype-equal overrides are canonicalized away. Network hash comparison must distinguish changed component values.
features.current: copy_with_count clones patch but assigns a new Bedrock uid. are_items_and_components_equal compares only patch entries, not the effective prototype-plus-patch map, and order/duplicate corner cases remain. BundleContentsImpl and ContainerImpl intentionally implement PartialEq as always false. features.expected: Official generic collection bounds are the passed max (often Integer.MAX_VALUE); specific components provide their own limits, e.g. ItemLore 256, HashedPatchMap map/set 256, changed slots 128. Length-prefixed component data is bounded by the codec max and decoded from an isolated slice; the official generic slice wrapper itself does not require nested reader exhaustion. Unknown registry IDs fail through registry lookup.
features.current: Current code rejects negative component counts and caps total ItemStack patch entries at 256, caps length-prefixed payloads at MAX_PACKET_DATA_SIZE, and adds many 128/256 component-specific ceilings. The normal read path casts component IDs with `as u8`, so a value above 255 can wrap before lookup. The length-prefixed reader decodes a bounded byte vector but does not check cursor exhaustion; this matches the official slice wrapper's lack of an explicit nested trailing check, while the local MAX_PACKET_DATA_SIZE is much narrower than official registryFriendlyLengthPrefixed(Integer.MAX_VALUE).
features.impact: The boundary is fail-closed for many negative/oversized inputs but can reject legal large values and has a wrapped-ID risk in the normal reader. Different component limits make compatibility dependent on the chosen path.
features.first_repro: Static input: normal ItemStackSerializer::read receives component ID VarInt(256). features.name: Serverbound chat packet versus unsigned/signed command routing
features.final_verdict_raw: confirmed packet-route/authentication-context difference; not privilege escalation or console execution
features.reason: The route mismatch is exact: Pumpkin handle_chat_message checks strip_prefix('/') and invokes handle_chat_command before validate_chat_message. Official handleChat applies last-seen state and tryHandleChat for a chat packet; unsigned and signed commands arrive through distinct packet methods. The Pumpkin command source remains the player source, parse_nodes/command dispatch remains permission-filtered, and no Console/Rcon source is installed. Thus the original P1 op/console-escalation claim is not supported, while the pre-validation packet-type/authentication-context difference remains confirmed.
features.expected: A ServerboundChatPacket is processed as chat: ACK is applied, the signed body is decoded/validated, then it is filtered/decorated/broadcast. Commands use the dedicated unsigned or signed command packet paths.
features.current: When SChatMessage.message starts with '/', handle_chat_message strips the prefix and calls handle_chat_command before validate_chat_message. A malicious or nonstandard client can therefore route a chat packet into the unsigned command path; the command's signable-argument check is not the same as validating the original chat packet.
features.impact: A client sends a Serverbound chat-message packet whose message starts with '/' and whose signature/ACK would otherwise be relevant. Pumpkin enters the player-permission-filtered command path before chat validation. Commands with signable arguments are rejected in secure mode; commands without signable arguments still require the player's effective permission and command tree. No console permission inheritance occurs.
features.first_repro: Static packet input: SChatMessage {message="/stop", signature=None or invalid, arbitrary timestamp/salt/ACK}. Official handleChat does not call handleChatCommand; Pumpkin strips '/' and calls handle_chat_command before validate_chat_message. Replace /stop with an already-permitted, non-signable-argument command for an action-bearing route check. No packet or runtime was run.

limitations: The inspected dispatcher still applies server-side permission checks; this finding is a packet-route/authenticity mismatch, not proof that a normal player obtains op permission.
No malicious wire client or server process was run.
limits.unconfirmed: No malicious wire client, command permission matrix, plugin event, or runtime dispatch was executed.
limits.impact_conditions: A client must send a Serverbound chat-message packet whose text begins with '/' rather than the dedicated unsigned/signed command packet. The observable difference is strongest with a missing/invalid chat signature or ACK: Pumpkin enters command parsing before validate_chat_message. In secure mode, commands with signable arguments are rejected by the unsigned-command gate; commands with no signable arguments still follow the player permission-filtered command path. With allow_chat_reports=false, this is additionally within Pumpkin's explicit unsigned-chat policy. Any command effect still requires the player's effective permission and the current command tree; no console permission inheritance occurs.

features.name: Preservation of validated signed message metadata through broadcast
features.reason: broadcast_secure_player_chat reconstructs link/index/last-seen from local cache rather than passing the validated inbound message. The metadata integrity difference is real, but metadata alone is not labeled disconnect/security.
features.expected: The exact validated PlayerChatMessage retains the incoming link index/session, content, timestamp, salt, signature, and resolved last-seen list when it reaches broadcast and outgoing packet serialization.
features.current: Validation verifies the incoming message but discards the resolved last_seen returned by apply_last_seen_update. broadcast_secure_player_chat reconstructs a new message using ChatSession.messages_sent as index, a nil session UUID, and sender.signature_cache.last_seen instead of the packet's resolved ACK list. Commands also consume inbound chain indices but do not advance messages_sent, so interleaving commands and chat can produce a different outgoing index.
features.first_repro: Static two-packet input: accept one signed command argument at inbound index 0, then a signed chat at inbound index 1 with nonempty ACK history. Current broadcast uses messages_sent=0 and sender.signature_cache.last_seen; official getSignedMessage/broadcast retains link index 1 and packet-resolved LastSeenMessages.

limitations: This is a source data-flow finding; no client-side signature verification was run.
Clientbound wire packets do not carry the session UUID directly, so the nil internal link is reported together with the independently confirmed index/last-seen reconstruction loss.

features.name: Serialization of validation, filtering, decoration, and broadcast order
features.reason: Independent spawn_task calls lack the official per-connection FutureChain after validation; ordering race is a static scheduling risk, not a runtime reproduction.
features.expected: Inbound chat packets may validate promptly, but filtering/decorating/broadcast side effects are appended to one per-connection FutureChain so accepted messages retain packet order.
features.current: Each SChatMessage is copied and submitted with server.spawn_task(async move { handle_chat_message }). The validation sidecar is locked transactionally, but event, decoration, broadcast, messages_sent increment, and recipient-cache mutations occur after that lock without a per-connection FutureChain. Concurrent tasks can reorder side effects and race the separate messages_sent read/increment.
features.first_repro: Static concurrency fixture: enqueue two accepted SChatMessage packets before either filter/event task completes. Official FutureChain appends callbacks in packet order; current independent spawn_task calls have no ordering edge after verify_and_commit and both can observe the same messages_sent value.

limitations: Tokio scheduling, plugin callback latency, and actual reordering were not measured because runtime/tests are prohibited.
The cryptographic acceptance cursor itself is serialized; the finding is the post-validation dispatch/broadcast phase.

features.name: Chat and command spam throttling and rejection timing
features.reason: Official listener has separate chat and command throttlers; current Player::check_chat_spam updates one shared counter despite SpamType. This is rate-policy divergence, not security proof.
features.expected: Vanilla keeps separate chat and command TickThrottler instances, increments the relevant one after the corresponding operation, decays them by tick, and disconnects non-operator/singleplayer-owner players after the configured threshold.
features.current: Pumpkin has separate SpamType labels and configurable thresholds/cost/decay, but both Java chat and command paths use the same Player.chat_spam_tick_count. Chat and command traffic therefore share one budget, and the current check occurs before chat broadcast or command dispatch completion.
features.first_repro: Static state matrix: send chat messages until the shared score is near threshold, then send a command. Official command throttler is unaffected by chat score; current shared chat_spam_tick_count crosses the same threshold. Reverse the order for the symmetric case.

limitations: The exact default official threshold value was not inferred beyond the TickThrottler fields; this finding is about separate counters and sequencing.

features.name: chunk batch start/finish flow and client batch acknowledgement rate
features.reason: Current batch rate clamp is 0.1..500.0 and NaN→0.1; official PlayerChunkSender uses 0.01..64.0 and NaN→0.01. This is a flow-control constant difference, not a disconnect claim.
features.expected: For 26.2 the sender emits Start, all chunk-with-light packets, and Finished in order; it limits unacknowledged batches to 1 initially and 10 after an acknowledgement. The desired rate is NaN/0.01..64.0 and the batch quota is adjusted only by the acknowledgement flow.
features.current: Pumpkin emits Start and Finished and tracks in-flight batches, but clamps a client rate to 0.1..500.0 (`MAX_CHUNKS_PER_TICK` 500) instead of the official 0.01..64.0. limits.limitations: The flow was compared from current source and official Java 25 bytecode only. Queue priority/order was not observed on a live connection and no client rendering/back-pressure result was measured.

features.name: relative movement range, forced position sync/teleport, and player teleport confirmation
features.final_verdict_raw: partial implementation; overflow branch statically present but runtime-unreproduced
features.reason: The official condition is confirmed: ServerEntity::sendChanges uses VecDeltaCodec.encodeX/Y/Z, requires every encoded axis to be within -32768..32767, forces ClientboundEntityPositionSyncPacket when out of range, when getRequiresPrecisePosition is true, or when teleportDelay exceeds 400, and otherwise emits Pos/PosRot. Current Entity::send_pos_rot computes delta*4096 and casts each axis directly to i16 before deciding whether position changed; it has no signed-short range test, precise-position branch, or forced-period branch. The original context was too broad about teleports, however. Explicit current teleport paths use absolute packets and bypass this cast: Entity::teleport emits CEntityPositionSync and updates last_sent_pos; Player::request_teleport emits CPlayerPosition and awaits confirmation; shulker/shulker-bullet special paths also emit CEntityPositionSync. send_pos_rot callers are normal movement/tick paths (living entities, items, falling blocks, TNT, minecarts, eye of ender, dragon/parts) and can also follow direct set_pos, not the dedicated teleport caller. Static source proves the missing guard and a potential wrap if a caller supplies a delta beyond the short range, but it does not prove that an ordinary current movement caller actually produces >32767/4096 between sends. No runtime packet was emitted.
features.expected: Relative deltas are sent only when each encoded axis fits signed short range; otherwise or on the official forced interval the server sends an absolute position-sync packet. Player corrective teleports install an id and accept only the matching confirmation before movement resumes.
features.current: Player corrections use a pending teleport id and matching confirmation guard. For non-player entities, Entity::send_pos_rot casts delta*4096 directly to i16 and emits relative packets without the official range check, precise-position handling, or 400-tick absolute sync path; no current CEntityPositionSync/teleport send path exists there. A large move can therefore wrap the wire delta instead of becoming an absolute sync.
features.impact: A tracked non-player entity must reach Entity::send_pos_rot with at least one axis delta whose encoded value is outside [-32768,32767], approximately an axis displacement of 8.0 blocks or more at the 1/4096 scale, or must require precise/periodic absolute synchronization. Dedicated teleport commands, cross-world teleports, player corrective teleports, shulker teleports, and shulker-bullet absolute updates are not this path. Ordinary movement callers usually advance once per tick; the exact velocity/plugin/entity state needed to cross the boundary was not statically bounded in this audit.
features.first_repro: Static boundary input: for a tracked non-player Entity, set last_sent_pos=(0,0,0), set pos=(8.0,0,0) immediately before send_pos_rot, and use a non-player entity type. Official ServerEntity selects ClientboundEntityPositionSyncPacket because encodeX is outside the signed-short range; current send_pos_rot casts 8.0*4096=32768 to i16 and proceeds through the relative packet path. This is a source-level fixture only; no Entity instance, packet serializer, client, or runtime result was run.

limits.limitations: The player confirmation path was read statically and not vanilla-client verified. The non-player overflow is derived from the current cast and official branch; no live packet decoder/client visual result was obtained.
limits.unconfirmed: No runtime movement, entity fixture, packet decode, vanilla client, or numeric bound for every current movement caller was measured.

features.name: entity movement/rotation/metadata recipient filtering versus tracking-player broadcast
features.reason: Movement/rotation call World::broadcast_to_chunk while official ServerEntity synchronizer targets seenBy tracking players. Recipient authority differs by packet type; no runtime recipient set was captured.
features.expected: Entity state packets are sent to the entity's seenBy/tracking set (and self only where the official method says so), not merely to every player whose watched chunk contains the entity chunk. Tracking range, spectator predicate, and pairing state must remain the recipient authority.
features.current: Entity::send_pos_rot and send_rotation use World::broadcast_to_chunk, which filters by watched-section distance but not the TrackedEntity.seen_by set or the entity's effective tracking range. Metadata dirty updates do consult seen_by, so recipient authority differs by packet type. A client can therefore receive movement/rotation for an entity outside its pairing set or receive movement without a corresponding spawn in an edge case.

features.name: frame length VarInt legal width, overlong encoding, and negative values
features.reason: Current VarInt::decode_async permits five bytes and get_raw_packet checks only after conversion; official Varint21FrameDecoder copyVarint rejects a third continuation byte. This is a static frame-boundary difference, not a runtime DoS proof.
features.expected: The network frame prefix is a nonzero VarInt21: at most 3 bytes, with a continuation bit in the third byte rejected as wider than 21 bits. A negative or otherwise invalid frame length must not become a readable frame.
features.current: Pumpkin's VarInt decoder accepts up to 5 bytes and get_raw_packet casts the i32 result to u64 before checking 0..=MAX_PACKET_SIZE. Four-byte values up to the configured limit can therefore reach the frame-length check; negative values are rejected only after conversion as out of bounds.

features.name: PacketDecoder exact payload consumption and trailing bytes
features.final_verdict_raw: confirmed difference on the known SPlayerLoaded play path; not an every-packet acceptance claim
features.reason: Official PacketDecoder::decode invokes the protocol codec and throws IOException when readableBytes remains before delivering the packet. Pumpkin TCPNetworkDecoder returns the post-id bytes as RawPacket.payload, and JavaClient::handle_play_packet has no final residual check. The exact SPlayerLoaded reader ignores its input and its play branch returns without require_empty_body, so a valid SPlayerLoaded ID plus one trailing byte is a statically sufficient uncovered path. This is the same trailing-byte root as NET-PLAY-DISPATCH-05, not a separate defect.
features.expected: After the official packet codec decodes a packet, any remaining bytes in the frame cause IOException; the packet is not delivered as valid.
features.current: TCPNetworkDecoder returns all bytes after packet-id as RawPacket.payload. Some callers explicitly invoke require_empty_body, including status and selected configuration/chat paths, but handle_play_packet has no generic post-deserialization empty-body check and many branches do not call one. Trailing payload acceptance therefore depends on each caller.
features.impact: A valid protocol-776 play packet reaches a branch whose reader succeeds while leaving payload bytes, and that branch has no local or common residual check. The finding does not state that status, reconfiguration, or every play packet accepts trailing bytes; several current callers explicitly check the remainder.
features.first_repro: Static minimal input: protocol 776 SPlayerLoaded packet ID with payload [0x00]. SPlayerLoaded::read returns Ok without consuming bytes; handle_play_packet's SPlayerLoaded branch has no generic require_empty_body, while official PacketDecoder checks readableBytes and throws before delivery. No packet injection or disconnect observation was run.

limits.limitations: This is a confirmed architectural difference, not a claim that every current play packet handler accepts trailing data. The exact affected packet set requires a per-handler audit.
limits.unconfirmed: No packet injection, runtime rejection/acceptance, or exhaustive per-packet generated-code enumeration was run.
limits.impact_conditions: A packet must have a valid packet id and a generated/current ServerPacket::read implementation that succeeds while leaving one or more bytes in the payload, and it must enter a caller without a branch-local or common residual check. This is not a claim that every play packet accepts trailing data; status, reconfiguration, selected configuration, signed chat-command, and configuration-ack paths have explicit checks.

features.name: Login packet state gates, duplicate/late LoginStart and LoginAcknowledged
features.reason: Current dispatcher lacks the complete official login phase gate for repeated LoginStart/early LoginAcknowledged, while verify-token absence is rejected. This is state confusion, not an authentication bypass finding.
features.expected: 26.2 vanilla gates Hello to HELLO, Key to KEY, Login Acknowledged to PROTOCOL_SWITCHING, and progresses through HELLO -> KEY -> AUTHENTICATING -> NEGOTIATING/VERIFYING -> WAITING_FOR_DUPE_DISCONNECT -> PROTOCOL_SWITCHING -> ACCEPTED. features.current: Pumpkin has packet/state separation but no login-phase flag for LoginStart or LoginAcknowledged. PendingConnection::handle_login_packet dispatches both whenever connection_state is Login; LoginStart can be handled again and LoginAcknowledged is accepted before a LoginSuccess/profile exists. verify_encryption_token does reject an encryption response without a pending token, so this is not an unconditional crypto bypass.
features.first_repro: Static fixture: in Login state send Login Acknowledged before LoginStart, or send a second LoginStart after the first request. Expected official state error; current dispatcher reaches handle_login_acknowledged/handle_login_start. No network/server run performed.

limitations: The early LoginAcknowledged path later stops when no GameProfile exists, so this evidence establishes state confusion/late-packet acceptance, not authentication bypass.

raw_record.current: Pumpkin bounds LoginStart name to 16, rejects control/space, and in online mode replaces the initial client UUID/profile with the hasJoined profile. It serializes name, UUID, and properties. The 26.2 session_id is generated with Uuid::new_v4() per login, whereas vanilla passes MinecraftServer.getConnection().getSessionId(), a server-session value. This is a protocol/identity difference but not evidence of a forged authenticated UUID.
raw_record.first_reproduction: Compare two sequential successful 26.2 LoginSuccess packets: official LoginFinished.sessionId is sourced from the server connection session; Pumpkin finish_login writes a fresh UUID each time. Static comparison only; no client run.
limitations: The client-visible semantic importance of session_id in 26.2 was not runtime-probed.
Username validation is treated as equivalent from the bytecode boundary; no exhaustive Unicode/property test was run.

features.name: Offline-mode UUID and profile construction
features.reason: offline_uuid hashes the username directly with SHA-256, while official UUIDUtil uses UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes(OfflinePlayer:<name>). This breaks vanilla offline-file compatibility; offline-mode impersonation is not promoted to P1/P0.
features.expected: When online authentication is disabled, derive UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes("OfflinePlayer:" + username in UTF-8), then create the offline GameProfile. This is an intentional unauthenticated-name limitation, not an online-auth failure.
features.current: offline_uuid computes SHA-256(username)[0..16] and constructs a UUID directly. Both offline login and Bungee fallback reuse this value, so Pumpkin is internally consistent but incompatible with vanilla offline UUIDs and existing vanilla ops/whitelist/ban files.
features.first_repro: For username Steve compare UUIDUtil.createOfflinePlayerUUID("Steve") with Pumpkin offline_uuid("Steve"). Expected official uses UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes("OfflinePlayer:Steve"), current uses SHA-256 first 16 bytes. Pure static/code comparison; not executed.

limitations: Offline-mode name impersonation remains an intentional property of offline mode and is not counted as a P0/P1 authentication bypass here.
No migration impact on an existing Pumpkin world was measured.
limits.unconfirmed: migration impact not measured

features.name: RSA challenge, verify token, shared secret, AES stream setup, and nonce terminology
features.reason: RSA 1024-bit, four-byte verify token, 16-byte AES secret, SHA-1 server digest, PKCS#1 v1.5, and AES-CFB8 key/IV setup align with the official Crypt/ServerboundKeyPacket path.
features.expected: For online login use a 1024-bit RSA keypair, random 4-byte challenge, 128-bit AES secret, RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption/verification, SHA-1 digest over serverId/secret/public-key bytes, then encrypted stream setup. A standalone SignedNonce class is not present in the selected 26.2 artifact; Crypt$SaltSignaturePair is an actual salt/signature record, not the login challenge.
features.current: Pumpkin generates one 1024-bit RSA keypair per server, sends DER public key and a random 4-byte token, decrypts both RSA payloads with PKCS#1 v1.5, requires a 16-byte shared secret, computes SHA-1 over empty serverId + secret + public-key DER, and upgrades both directions to AES-128-CFB8 with key-as-IV. The current-version 26.2 path consumes the verify token; the omission compatibility branch is restricted to 1.19.3..1.20.0. Static crypto construction matches the official contract.
features.first_repro: Static parameter comparison: KeyStore RSA bits=1024, token=4 bytes, shared secret=16 bytes, auth_digest=SHA-1 signed BigInt, decoder/encoder AES CFB8 key=IV versus Crypt bytecode. No secret, token, or credential was stored.

limitations: No cryptographic round-trip or official client handshake was executed.
No SignedNonce actual class was found by jar inventory; this is absence of a named class, not a claim that no nonce-like field exists anywhere.
limits.unconfirmed: no cryptographic round trip

features.name: Sessionserver hasJoined verification, digest, optional IP, failure handling, and profile replacement
features.reason: hasJoined call/result mapping and fail-closed branches exist. Address selection and proxy configuration differ, but no external auth request was made and no identity bypass is established.
features.expected: After the key handshake, call sessionService.hasJoinedServer(username, SHA-1 digest, remote address only when prevent-proxy policy requires it); accept the returned GameProfile, otherwise fail closed in multiplayer. The returned UUID/name/properties become the authenticated identity.
features.current: Pumpkin calls the Mojang-compatible hasJoined URL with the same digest and replaces the provisional profile on HTTP 200. HTTP 204 becomes UnverifiedUsername and transport/server failures become FailedResponse. The default URL includes IP only when prevent_proxy_connections is enabled; custom URL/fallback support is extra. The address is self.address, so Bungee's dropped forwarded IP affects this when IP-bound auth is configured.
features.first_repro: Use a no-HTTP fixture for status mapping: 200 profile -> replacement, 204 -> UnverifiedUsername, server/network error -> FailedResponse; compare URL with and without prevent_proxy_connections. External HTTP probe intentionally not performed.

limitations: No external sessionserver access or HTTP mock execution was performed.
The exact authlib implementation of hasJoinedServer was represented by ServerLoginPacketListenerImpl$1.run invocation evidence; no external authlib dependency was copied.
limits.unconfirmed: HTTP/sessionserver and proxy-address matrix not executed

features.name: Vanilla online/offline configuration distinction and authentication.enabled semantics
features.reason: Java login branches on networking.java.online_mode and config validation requires encryption for online mode. AuthenticationConfig.enabled is a separate Pumpkin setting and is not used by this Java branch; this is a configuration semantic mismatch, not proof of online-auth bypass.
features.expected: With vanilla online-mode conditions matched, Hello enters RSA/session verification; with offline-mode conditions matched, no auth challenge is required and UUIDUtil.createOfflineProfile is used. Invalid online_mode=true/encryption=false should not be treated as a valid online configuration.
features.current: Pumpkin's online_mode selector matches the two broad branches and config validation asserts encryption when online_mode is true. However Java login never consults AuthenticationConfig.enabled; online_mode alone controls the sessionserver call. Proxy-enabled branches also use proxy forwarding instead of the ordinary online/offline branch. Therefore an operator setting authentication.enabled=false does not disable Java authentication, while online_mode=false remains intentionally unauthenticated.
features.first_repro: Static matrix: (online_mode=true,encryption=true), (online_mode=false,encryption=false), and (online_mode=true,encryption=false). Expected first two are meaningful branches and the third is rejected by config validation; authentication.enabled is not read by the Java login path. No config load or server start was run.

limitations: Proxy mode is an intentional Pumpkin extension and is not labelled unsupported merely because vanilla has no Velocity/Vine/Bungee branch.
No assertion path was executed.
limits.unconfirmed: full config-load matrix not executed

features.name: Profile properties, texture validation, profile actions, and LoginFinished property transport
features.reason: Authenticated profile properties are carried into LoginFinished; extra local texture policy is not a missing vanilla listener contract.
features.expected: Use the authenticated GameProfile, including UUID, name, and profile properties, in LoginFinished. Vanilla's session service result is trusted as the profile source; no separate login-time local texture-domain policy is required by the vanilla listener.
features.current: Pumpkin preserves returned properties and sends them in LoginSuccess/LoginFinished. It additionally decodes the textures property and applies configured scheme/domain/type policy, and rejects disallowed profile actions according to AuthenticationConfig. This is an extra policy boundary, not evidence that vanilla secure-profile verification is absent; the current code does not independently verify a texture signature against Mojang profile-property keys.
features.first_repro: Static path trace: HTTP-200 GameProfile properties -> texture/profile-action validation -> CLoginSuccess properties list. Compare official LoginFinished GameProfile codec. No signed-property fixture was executed.

limitations: The selected official server listener delegates profile authenticity to authlib/session service; profile-property signature verification was not separately reconstructed.
Texture URL policy is Pumpkin configuration behavior and was not classified as a vanilla mismatch.

features.name: Compression threshold, compressed/uncompressed frame semantics, and encryption/decompression ordering
features.reason: Login-relevant compression threshold, declared length, and decrypt-before-decompress ordering match the official encoder/decoder evidence.
features.expected: Compression is inclusive at threshold: data length >= threshold is zlib-compressed; data length 0 in the compressed framing denotes an uncompressed packet below threshold. Decode must enforce the advertised decompressed length and use decrypt-before-decompress stream order.
features.current: Pumpkin encoder uses data_len >= threshold, decoder rejects uncompressed data at/above threshold, enforces MAX_PACKET_DATA_SIZE=8,388,608, and reads the declared payload length exactly. DecryptionReader wraps the stream before decompression. These static rules match the official threshold/length contract for the inspected path.
features.first_repro: Static boundary comparison at threshold=5: official CompressionEncoder uses if data length < threshold for uncompressed; Pumpkin uses >= for compression and decoder rejects data_len >= threshold when uncompressed. No test command was run.

limitations: No zlib trailing-stream or live TCP differential was run in this audit.
Outer Pumpkin MAX_PACKET_SIZE is a separate framing policy and was not promoted to an auth finding.
limits.unconfirmed: no live handshake

features.name: Set Compression ordering relative to RSA response, AES enablement, session verification, and LoginSuccess
features.reason: Current login enables compression before the encryption request; official bytecode installs it later around authenticated login completion. Ordering difference is static only and is not by itself a security/disconnect claim.
features.expected: Vanilla 26.2 performs key verification/AES setup, completes session authentication, then sends LoginCompression (and installs compression after send) before LoginFinished. The LoginFinished packet is the transition into protocol switching.
features.current: For direct login, Pumpkin sends CSetCompression immediately from handle_login_start, installs compression before sending the encryption request, then later enables AES and performs session authentication. finish_login sends CLoginSuccess after that. This is a confirmed ordering difference from the official static path; it is not by itself proof of insecure plaintext after AES or of auth bypass.
features.first_repro: Compare call order: Pumpkin handle_login_start -> enable_compression -> encryption_request; official handleHello -> Hello, handleKey -> setEncryptionKey/authentication, verifyLoginAndFinishConnectionSetup -> LoginCompression callback -> LoginFinished. No client interoperability claim was made.

limitations: The client may accept both orderings; no official Java 26.2 client was started, so this remains a static confirmed difference, not a compatibility failure.
No P0/P1 security conclusion is drawn from order alone.
limits.unconfirmed: client interoperability not executed

features.name: Login plugins, transaction IDs, and login/config/play cookies
features.reason: Proxy extensions exist, but Velocity response ID binding and vanilla unsolicited cookie/query rejection are incomplete. HMAC/other checks remain; no forged identity is established.
features.expected: Vanilla login listener rejects an unsolicited custom-query answer or login cookie response as unexpected. Cookie payloads are bounded at 5120 bytes; query payloads are bounded at 1 MiB. Extension implementations must match the outstanding request/transaction before trusting a response.
features.current: Pumpkin intentionally supports proxy login plugins. Velocity sends a random message ID but receive_velocity_plugin_response does not compare response.message_id (the source has an explicit TODO); HMAC authenticates the payload. Vine uses a signed challenge nonce. With no supported proxy, an unsolicited login plugin response is ignored rather than disconnected. Login cookie responses are decoded/logged without request/key state; config/play cookie handlers similarly do not establish a vanilla request ledger. Protocol payload caps exist for several packets, but the login handler has no semantic request check.
features.first_repro: Static fixture: send a ServerboundCustomQueryAnswer/ServerboundCookieResponse without an outstanding server request. Official handle methods disconnect; Pumpkin login cookie logs/returns None and no-proxy plugin response returns None. No packet/server run performed.

limitations: Proxy login plugins are an intentional extension; the finding is the missing transaction/request binding, not the existence of proxy support.
No claim is made that the unbound Velocity response alone forges identity because its HMAC still covers the payload.
limits.unconfirmed: proxy/plugin packet runtime not executed

features.name: LoginSuccess/LoginAcknowledged and Login -> Configuration migration
features.reason: Normal LoginSuccess→Config gates exist, but early LoginAcknowledged is not equivalent to official PROTOCOL_SWITCHING. Existing no-profile guard limits the observed static consequence; no authenticated Play transition is claimed.
features.expected: Send terminal LoginFinished, accept LoginAcknowledged only while switching protocols, install the configuration listener, then require the server-requested known-packs/resource-pack sequence before Finish Configuration acknowledgment.
features.current: Normal Pumpkin flow sends CLoginSuccess, waits for LoginAcknowledged, enters Config, gates Known Packs/resource-pack/Finish with ConfigurationPhase, and only returns ReadyToPlay after a valid Finish acknowledgment. The normal config gates are a match. The migration entry itself is not guarded by a phase representing LoginSuccess/protocol switching, so an early LoginAcknowledged can move the connection to Config and emit configuration packets before a profile exists; the later finish path stops rather than granting play.
features.first_repro: Send LoginAcknowledged before the server has sent LoginSuccess. Expected official Validate.validState failure/disconnect; current handle_login_acknowledged stores Config and continues sending brand/known-packs until a later no-profile stop. Static only.

limitations: This is a state/protocol issue; current no-profile guard prevents a direct authenticated Play transition in the inspected path.
The old network audit claim about configuration gates was rechecked at HEAD; current known-packs/resource/finish guards exist, while the LoginAcknowledged entry guard remains separate.

features.name: Duplicate UUID/name login behavior and old-session replacement
features.reason: Current duplicate UUID/name path rejects the new login; official waits for old-session disconnect and replaces it. This is policy/behavior difference, not data-loss or security proof.
features.expected: After authentication and admission checks, vanilla disconnects all existing players with the authenticated profile UUID, waits for duplicate disconnect completion, then sends LoginFinished for the new connection.
features.current: Pumpkin checks current UUID and current name before finish_login and rejects the new connection with duplicate-login text. Server::add_player contains replacement/chat-owner retirement machinery, but the pending login duplicate checks prevent the vanilla old-session replacement path from being reached for the same identity.
features.first_repro: With an existing player UUID/name, complete a second static authenticated profile path. Official calls disconnectAllPlayersWithProfile and waits; Pumpkin returns duplicate-login Stop before finish_login. No server or client was started.

limitations: The audit does not claim duplicate replacement is a security vulnerability; it is a vanilla behavior difference and may be an intentional product choice.
Runtime race behavior of old-session teardown was not observed.

features.name: Pre-login timeout, slow trickle behavior, and late-packet handling
features.reason: Official has a whole-login 600-tick ceiling; current per-read 30-second timeout resets on traffic. Slow trickle can therefore survive longer statically, but resource impact was not measured.
features.expected: Vanilla increments one login tick counter and disconnects at 600 ticks (30 seconds at the normal 20 TPS) if login has not completed. Unexpected packets/states are rejected; login does not gain an unbounded lease by sending one packet before each timeout.
features.current: PendingConnection::get_packet creates a 30-second sleep for each read and resets it after every decoded packet. A peer that trickles valid packets can therefore extend the pre-login lifetime beyond the official whole-login 600-tick ceiling. Packet rate limiting exists, and post-login keep-alive/activity timeouts exist, but they are not the same pending-login deadline.
features.first_repro: Static timing fixture: send one syntactically valid login packet every 29 seconds without completing auth. Official tick reaches 600 and disconnects; current per-read idle timer resets. No timer test was run.

limitations: Tokio scheduling and packet-limiter interaction were not measured.
The 30-second official value is derived from MAX_TICKS_BEFORE_LOGIN=600 in bytecode and the standard server tick contract; no vanilla runtime was started.
limits.unconfirmed: slow-trickle connection not run

Packet rate limiting exists, and post-login keep-alive/activity timeouts exist, but they are not the same pending-login deadline.
raw_record.first_reproduction: Static timing fixture: send one syntactically valid login packet every 29 seconds without completing auth. Official tick reaches 600 and disconnects; current per-read idle timer resets. No timer test was run.
limitations: Tokio scheduling and packet-limiter interaction were not measured.
The 30-second official value is derived from MAX_TICKS_BEFORE_LOGIN=600 in bytecode and the standard server tick contract; no vanilla runtime was started.

features.name: Proxy identity forwarding and proxy authentication: BungeeGuard, Velocity HMAC, Vine signature/nonce
features.reason: BungeeCord returns a verified forwarded IP but current login discards it as _ip before canonical admission/auth checks; Velocity ID comparison also has a source TODO. This is an authenticated proxy identity-boundary discrepancy, not proof of forgeability without runtime/config conditions.
features.expected: Vanilla has no Bungee/Velocity/Vine forwarding protocol. Where proxy forwarding is deliberately enabled as an extension, the backend must authenticate the proxy payload before trusting forwarded UUID/profile/IP, and all IP-based admission/auth checks should use the authenticated client IP rather than the proxy socket.
features.current: BungeeCord parses forwarded IP/UUID/properties and optionally requires exactly one BungeeGuard token, but handle_login_start binds the profile and discards the returned forwarded IP as _ip; can_not_join and pre-login therefore use the proxy socket address. Velocity validates HMAC-SHA256 and updates address/profile, but does not bind the response message ID. Vine validates Ed25519, version, timestamp drift <=30 seconds, and a per-connection 16-byte challenge, then updates address/profile. The extension authentication mechanisms are present; Bungee identity propagation and Velocity transaction binding are incomplete.
features.first_repro: Bungee static matrix: bungeecord_login returns 192.0.2.10 for a socket at 10.0.0.1, but caller stores only profile and leaves PendingConnection.address at 10.0.0.1; can_not_join then checks the wrong IP. Velocity static matrix: valid HMAC payload with an unrelated response.message_id is not rejected by receive_velocity_plugin_response. No proxy was run.

limitations: Official vanilla does not define these proxy extensions; the P1 is limited to the current authenticated-forwarding trust boundary, not a vanilla feature absence.
A Bungee configuration with an empty secret is intentionally spoofable by direct connections and is not silently counted as secure proxy authentication.
No P0 conclusion is warranted from static proxy evidence.

features.name: unknown packet IDs and generic packet read/dispatch failure behavior
features.reason: TCPNetworkDecoder emits RawPacket for an id without resolving a typed codec. JavaClient::handle_play_packet falls through on an unknown play id, logs a warning, and returns Ok(()); Player::process_inbound_packets therefore does not enter the kick path for that case. Official PacketDecoder resolves through ProtocolInfo.codec before listener delivery, and Connection handles invalid processing by disconnecting. This confirms the unknown-play-id boundary only; known decode errors are a separate path.
features.expected: The official protocol codec resolves a packet type before listener dispatch. Unknown or undecodable IDs raise a decoder/packet error; Connection handles invalid processing by disconnecting rather than silently accepting an unhandled play ID.
features.current: Handshake, status, login, and configuration defaults return ReadingError and are kicked by their callers. In contrast, JavaClient::handle_play_packet logs `Failed to handle player packet id` in its default branch and returns Ok(()); Player::process_inbound_packets therefore treats an unknown play ID as handled. The java_packet macro only emits MultiVersionJavaPacket::to_id and does not generate field reading or dispatch.

features.reason: Current readers contain concrete guards for several enum values, signed-command counts, changed-slot counts, game-rule counts, and key lengths.
