features.name: bundle delimiters, FIFO ordering, frame batching, and flush behavior
features.reason: Official GameProtocols has bundle metadata and Connection installs PacketBundlePacker/PacketBundleUnpacker. Current Pumpkin has a bundle delimiter type but no CBundleDelimiter call site, and the sole egress path drains FIFO packets, frames them individually, writes batches, and flushes; frame batching is not semantic bundle packing/unpacking. Ordinary FIFO ordering and flush behavior are present, so this remains a bounded partial implementation finding.
features.expected: Official ProtocolInfo carries BundlerInfo; protocol setup installs packer/unpacker around bundle delimiters. Connection preserves queued packet ordering, writes through the channel, and flushes according to the send/flush lifecycle.
features.current: Pumpkin has the bundle-delimiter packet type and a single FIFO outgoing queue. The writer drains batches, splits batches at MAX_FRAME_BATCH_DATA_SIZE, frames each packet separately, writes the complete frame buffer, then flushes once per batch. No equivalent generic PacketBundlePacker/Unpacker installation or automatic bundle grouping was found; ordinary FIFO/write-all/flush ordering is present.
features.first_repro: Queue multiple bundle-eligible clientbound packets and compare the wire sequence with official ProtocolInfo BundlerInfo behavior. Static current path emits individually framed packets through the FIFO writer; no bundle packer/unpacker call is present.
existing_tests: No automatic bundle pack/unpack test was found.

limits.limitations: The exact official bundle-eligible packet set and a wire capture were not reconstructed or executed.

features.name: keep-alive challenge validation, ping response, and timeout policy
features.reason: Official common keep-alive policy uses a 15,000 ms interval, one pending challenge, and disconnects on a wrong response while pending. Current Pumpkin defaults to 15 seconds but permits configuration, stores up to 16 pending IDs, accepts any matching old pending ID, ignores wrong/duplicate IDs, and adds a roughly 2*configured-interval inactivity timeout. Play and reconfiguration response handlers are present, but this policy is not equivalent; initial PendingConnection configuration has no matching keep-alive branch. No timeout or wrong-ID runtime result was measured.
features.expected: Vanilla sends a keep-alive after 15,000 ms, disconnects when a prior challenge remains pending at the next interval, accepts only the current challenge ID, updates latency, and handles ping packets through their listener method.
features.current: Pumpkin uses the configured keep_alive_time interval, tracks up to 16 pending IDs, updates ping for any matching pending ID, ignores unexpected/duplicate IDs, and times out on a pending response, wait_for_keep_alive age, or any-packet inactivity after roughly 2*keep_alive_time. Play ping request is decoded as i64 and answered with CPingResponse; config keep-alive has a parallel response path.
features.first_repro: Send an old or duplicated keep-alive ID while a different challenge is pending. Official handleKeepAlive disconnects when keepAlivePending is true and the ID does not match; current JavaClient logs and ignores the ID. Configure keep_alive_time other than 15 seconds to exercise the policy difference.
existing_tests: No keep-alive timeout or wrong-ID runtime test was run.

limits.limitations: No wall-clock timeout, wrong-id, duplicate-id, or initial-configuration keep-alive fixture was run.

features.name: EOF, malformed-frame termination, disconnect notification, and player cleanup

features.reason: The current static path is complete enough to trace: TCPNetworkDecoder::get_raw_packet -> JavaClient::progress_player_packets -> Player::inbound_packets -> Player::process_inbound_packets (maximum 64 per tick) -> PacketReceivedEvent -> JavaClient::handle_play_packet -> typed reader and handler. features.name: registration mapping versus actual field-layout/codec parity
features.reason: The 256-entry/0-mismatch result is a registration mapping result only. The java_packet macro generates numeric to_id mapping, while each ServerPacket::read and ClientPacket::write_packet_data is handwritten. The inspected official ProtocolInfo/GameProtocols evidence does not establish complete field order, widths, enum/count constraints, version gates, consumed length, or side-effect parity for all 256 entries. This is a verified scope boundary, not a confirmed schema mismatch and not a P0.
features.expected: A packet ID mapping match must be followed by independent comparison of field order, field width, enum/count constraints, version gates, trailing-byte behavior, and state-side effects for each packet codec.
features.current: The java_packet macro emits only the versioned numeric to_id implementation; each packet's read/write layout is handwritten in separate modules. The available GameProtocols/ProtocolInfo evidence establishes registration and codec ownership but does not expose a complete field-by-field equivalence proof for all 256 entries. Several readers and dispatch handlers have already shown independent validation/trailing-byte boundaries, so no mapping result is promoted to a layout match.

features.current: Pumpkin checks max_players before constructing/validating the final profile and has no operator bypass in that check. features.name: online/offline authentication owner, proxy-forwarded identity trust, BungeeCord/Velocity/Vine verification, and forwarded IP ownership
features.reason: Proxy forwarding is outside the vanilla Java denominator; retain only as extension trust-boundary review.
features.expected: Vanilla 26.2 has online/offline mode and a prevent-proxy-connections property; it does not define BungeeCord, Velocity, or Vine forwarding. In online mode the session service owns the authenticated profile, while a proxy-forwarded profile is not a vanilla contract.
features.current: Pumpkin selects proxy forwarding before ordinary Java auth. BungeeCord accepts forwarded IP/UUID/profile and only rejects direct/mismatched data when a BungeeGuard secret is configured; Velocity verifies HMAC-SHA256; Vine verifies Ed25519, timestamp, and a 16-byte challenge. The Bungee caller discards the returned forwarded IP for admission checks. authentication.enabled is not the Java online-mode selector; online_mode controls session authentication.
features.impact: Proxy mode is outside the vanilla Java denominator. With Bungee secret empty, a directly connected peer can submit forwarding-shaped handshake data; with a configured proxy, IP-ban semantics use the proxy socket instead of the forwarded address. These are trust-boundary concerns, not vanilla compatibility claims.
features.first_repro: Static direct-connection input: proxy.enabled=true, bungeecord.enabled=true, secret=empty, and server_address containing forwarded UUID/profile. bungeecord_login accepts the data. Static owner input: authentication.enabled=false with java.online_mode=true; Java login still calls authenticate.

limitations: Proxy protocols are intentionally excluded from the Java 26.2 vanilla feature denominator.
No forged proxy handshake, live auth request, or network runtime was run.

features.name: 20 TPS scheduling, dynamic tickrate, freeze/step/sprint, pause-when-empty, overload catch-up, and watchdog termination
features.reason: Raw static claim retained only to the inspected symbols; no runtime equivalence or severity beyond the concrete user impact was established.
features.expected: Vanilla separates connection/tick processing from game ticking, supports freeze/step/sprint and dynamic rate, pauses after pause-when-empty seconds, warns and advances the schedule when overloaded, and runs a watchdog against max-tick-time that writes a crash report and forcibly exits.
features.current: Pumpkin implements rate/freeze/step/sprint and sends ticking state/step packets. features.name: server-thread packet ordering, scheduled task execution, plugin/datapack task ordering, and parallel world work
features.reason: Raw static claim retained only to the inspected symbols; no runtime equivalence or severity beyond the concrete user impact was established.
features.expected: Vanilla queues/processes packets, runs server-thread tasks, and executes tick logic on the authoritative server event loop with explicit wait/ordering points. Connection ticks are part of that controlled loop.
features.current: Pumpkin accepts Java connections on Tokio tasks, advances the dedicated Ticker thread, fires tick-start hooks, executes datapack tick functions, WASM scheduled tasks, scheduled functions, parallel world ticks, and player-data saves. TaskScheduler pops due tasks in heap order but dispatches each guest call through server.spawn_task; world/player/entity work also uses Rayon/Tokio runtime entry guards.
features.impact: Plugin scheduled callbacks and network-adjacent state changes are not proven to have vanilla single-thread ordering. Two due WASM tasks and parallel world work may complete in a different order than their heap insertion or vanilla server-thread order.
features.first_repro: Static two-task input: two due ScheduledTask entries at the same next_tick. Pumpkin collects them in heap iteration/pop order then spawns independent async guest calls; no join/order barrier is present before the next task/world phase.

limitations: No deterministic task-order fixture or runtime was run.
Parallelism itself is not classified as a bug without a state-level differential trace; the confirmed difference is the missing completion/order barrier.
open_questions: Which plugin APIs require main-thread affinity and which are intentionally concurrent.

features.reason: Raw static claim retained only to the inspected symbols; no runtime equivalence or severity beyond the concrete user impact was established.

features.name: Java status request/ping exposure, GS4 query challenge/status exposure, RCON authentication/command execution, and shutdown of exposure surfaces
features.reason: Raw static claim retained only to the inspected symbols; no runtime equivalence or severity beyond the concrete user impact was established.
features.expected: Vanilla handles one status request per status connection, replies to ping then disconnects, uses GS4 challenge binding/cache, refuses invalid/empty RCON configuration, and stops RCON clients/socket during server shutdown.
features.current: Pumpkin status has no per-connection has_requested_status gate, so repeated status requests are accepted; ping closes the connection. Query binds UDP with challenge tokens bound to SocketAddr and clears the map every 30 seconds; full status includes active plugin names. RCON refuses an empty password, supports max_connections and authentication, but each client is tokio::spawn'd outside Server::tasks and there is no explicit client-list shutdown. Startup also warns that RCON is plaintext/insecure.
features.impact: Status protocol behavior differs on repeated requests. RCON/query exposure has useful guards but shutdown can leave per-client tasks/connections outside the server task tracker, and query/status can expose Pumpkin plugin/runtime metadata beyond the Java vanilla contract.
features.first_repro: Static status input: send a second ServerboundStatusRequestPacket on one connection. Vanilla ServerStatusPacketListenerImpl disconnects after the first; Pumpkin handle_status_request sends another response. Static shutdown input: RCON listener task stops on STOP_INTERRUPT, but its inner client tokio::spawn handles are not tracked or joined.

limitations: No status/query/RCON socket was opened; no network or HTTP command was run.
The exact RCON packet parser bounds were out of scope for this row.
open_questions: Whether repeated status requests are intentionally tolerated for proxy/client compatibility.
Whether RCON client tasks are guaranteed to terminate when the runtime drops.

features.name: Play to Configuration trigger, world removal, Start Configuration, and outbound protocol switch
features.reason: If JavaClient::start_reconfiguration is invoked for a world-visible Play player, the source-contract difference remains: official switchToConfig sets waitingForSwitchToConfig, calls removePlayerFromWorld, sends Start Configuration, and calls Connection.setupOutboundProtocol(ConfigurationProtocols.CLIENTBOUND); Pumpkin claims ReconfigurationAwaitingStart, increments egress_epoch, and queues a StartConfiguration marker without world removal or protocol-pipeline setup. The production impact must be qualified downward because the exact caller inventory found the definition and test/doc references but no in-repo production caller. No equivalent suppression was found elsewhere: the phase/epoch gate protects outbound ordering only; connection_state remains Play during the trigger, progress_player_packets queues late non-ACK packets into Player::inbound_packets, World::tick continues, and Player::tick/process_inbound_packets continues for world members. Thus the missing remove/transition is not disproved by epoch flags or player late-callers, but active reachability is not established.
features.expected: When reconfiguration is requested, vanilla marks the switch pending, removes the player from the world, sends ClientboundStartConfigurationPacket, and changes the Connection outbound protocol to Configuration before configuration traffic continues.
features.current: Pumpkin accepts only Java versions supporting Configuration and only from Play, claims ReconfigurationAwaitingStart, increments egress_epoch, enqueues a StartConfiguration marker through the single writer, and then records ReconfigurationAwaitingAck. It does not remove the Player from World membership and does not call a protocol-pipeline setup equivalent; state is selected by the shared reader/writer dispatch.
features.impact: Only when the public start_reconfiguration trigger is reached for an established, world-visible Java Play player. Under that condition the player remains in World membership and continues through World::tick/Player::tick while the writer barrier changes outbound phase; late Play packets can still be queued and processed because connection_state is not changed by start_reconfiguration. If no production caller exists, this row is a latent/static compatibility difference rather than an active top issue.
features.first_repro: Static call input: established Play JavaClient with its Player published in world.players; invoke JavaClient::start_reconfiguration. Current path claims the phase and queues the marker only. Inspect the call graph: no production caller was found; tests/docs are not production reachability. If manually invoked, World::remove_player and Connection protocol setup are absent, while World::tick and Player::process_inbound_packets remain reachable. No runtime invocation was performed.

features.name: Configuration Acknowledged acceptance and inbound protocol/listener installation
features.reason: The ACK phase gate is present, but the official inbound listener/protocol installation is absent. Pumpkin claim_reconfiguration_ack accepts only ReconfigurationAwaitingAck, then stores ConnectionState::Config; JavaClient::progress_player_packets continues using the same TCPNetworkDecoder and state dispatch. Official Connection.setupInboundProtocol installs the Configuration protocol and a new ServerConfigurationPacketListenerImpl. This is a static architecture difference, not proof of a client-visible failure.
features.expected: A Configuration Acknowledged packet is legal only after a requested switch; vanilla rejects an unsolicited acknowledgement and installs a new ServerConfigurationPacketListenerImpl with the serverbound Configuration protocol on the same Connection.
features.current: Pumpkin atomically claims ReconfigurationAwaitingAck to AwaitingKnownPacks, kicks on a failed claim, stores ConnectionState::Config, and continues using the same TCP decoder with a state-based dispatch to handle_configuration_packet. There is no separate listener object or inbound protocol bind.
features.first_repro: Send Configuration Acknowledged in Play without a preceding successful Start Configuration marker, then send a Configuration packet. Pumpkin rejects the ACK through claim_reconfiguration_ack; for a valid ACK, Pumpkin changes state but never installs a Configuration protocol/listener as vanilla does.

limits.limitations: The Pumpkin kick path is static-only here; no client-visible disconnect was captured. The official protocol bind is established from bytecode, not a live Netty pipeline.

features.name: Egress epoch, phase writer barrier, FIFO ordering, and deferred Play packets
features.reason: The local epoch/FIFO barrier is genuinely present in current source, but static equivalence to the official channel synchronization cannot be established. The egress gate protects state capture, epoch increment, deferred Play packets, marker enqueue, stale-epoch checks, and finish ordering. Official Connection.syncAfterConfigurationChange synchronizes a channel future and protocol pipeline; it is not the same mechanism. No runtime race or channel-close behavior was measured.
features.expected: Packets captured before the switch must remain before the configuration marker; packets generated after the barrier must not cross into the old Play epoch, and protocol changes must synchronize with the channel write path.
features.current: Pumpkin has an explicit monotonically increasing egress_epoch, a mutex-protected EgressGate, one FIFO outgoing queue, packet state/phase/epoch metadata, and deferred_play release only after Finish acknowledgement. The writer validates marker epoch, packet IDs, phases, and finish ordering; this is a deliberate local barrier rather than the official Connection pipeline synchronization.
features.first_repro: Queue Play packets concurrently with start_reconfiguration and inspect writer metadata/order. Static inspection confirms a FIFO/epoch barrier and deferred queue, but does not prove equivalence to Connection::syncAfterConfigurationChange under a real channel close or protocol bind race.

limits.limitations: No test/build/runtime execution was allowed. The verdict covers ordering machinery only, not complete protocol semantics.

features.name: Known Packs negotiation and registry synchronization during reconfiguration
features.reason: The Known Packs comparison itself is ordered and exact, but the current caller passes the resulting selection to registry_entries_for_known_packs, whose _selection parameter is ignored and which always returns every static entry/payload. Official SynchronizeRegistriesTask.handleResponse uses the selected set for RegistrySynchronization ownership filtering and uses an empty set for fallback. The current direct async path also has no official ConfigurationTask queue. This is a static payload-contract difference, not a captured packet mismatch.

features.current: Pumpkin sends feature flags and Known Packs from Server::get_known_packs, remembers the request, then emits generated registry and tag tables. The path is a direct async handler with no ConfigurationTask queue; registry_entries_for_known_packs ignores Exact versus Fallback ownership selection, and the reconfiguration path does not itself invoke a fresh startConfiguration task sequence.

features.name: sector header, location/timestamp tables, length bounds, invalid sector handling
features.reason: Anvil rejects some out-of-range locations at region-loader scope while official RegionFile has per-entry validity handling.
features.expected: An Anvil region has an 8192-byte header containing 1024 offset entries and 1024 timestamps. A location packs a 24-bit sector offset and 8-bit sector count; chunk payload begins with a 4-byte length and one compression/version byte. Missing slots are absent, while truncated, out-of-range, non-positive, or malformed entries must not be read as valid payloads.
features.current: Pumpkin requires at least 8192 bytes, decodes the two tables, skips offset<2 or sector_count==0, rejects a payload extending beyond the available region bytes, and rejects length<1 or length beyond the allocated sector bytes. It does not detect overlapping allocated sectors; one out-of-range entry returns a region-level error rather than preserving other valid entries. Location packing is written with sector_count in the low byte.
features.first_repro: Static fixture: construct an 8192-byte header with one location pointing to a sector range beyond the file and another valid slot. Official RegionFile clears the invalid offset while retaining the table/other slots; current AnvilChunkFile::read returns ErrorDeserializingChunk for the first out-of-bounds entry and does not produce a usable serializer.

limitations: No .mca fixture was generated or parsed in this session.
Official RegionFile constructor's used-sector bookkeeping was inspected statically; overlap recovery was not runtime-observed.
The known upstream signed/offset underflow fix 334b37ade was only history/source-checked, not re-run.
limits.unconfirmed: No build/test/server/client/worldgen/runtime command was run; runtime_verified=false

features.name: compression IDs, external chunks, and oversized payloads
features.reason: Official 26.2 has external .mcc handling at the oversized-sector boundary; current Anvil writes in-region data and packs sector_count through an 8-bit location field.
features.expected: Official 26.2 recognizes IDs 1 gzip, 2 deflate, 3 none, 4 lz4, and 127 custom. Payloads requiring 256 or more sectors are stored in an external c.<x>.<z>.mcc file; the in-region stub has length 1 and the version byte with bit 0x80 set. The external stream is atomically moved into place and is removed by clear.
features.current: Pumpkin recognizes the same numeric IDs, but custom compression returns UnknownCompression. Default Anvil output is LZ4 level 6. There is no external .mcc path, no 0x80 external stub, and no oversized branch. AnvilChunkData::sector_count is u32, while location serialization truncates the count to the low 8 bits, so a payload at or above the vanilla external threshold cannot be represented safely in a normal .mca slot.
features.first_repro: Static input: serialize a chunk whose compressed payload needs 256 sectors. Official RegionFile::write switches to c.<chunkX>.<chunkZ>.mcc and writes an external stub; current AnvilChunkData::write emits the payload in place and AnvilChunkFile::write_indices packs sector_count into 8 bits.
existing_tests: crates/pumpkin-world/src/chunk/format/anvil.rs::Compression-related source paths (no dedicated oversized test found)

limitations: No large payload was generated, so the truncation consequence is static only.
The official custom compressor is intentionally unsupported by both the current default and this audit; only its ID/error boundary was compared.

features.name: block-state palette, biome palette, section bounds, heightmaps, and light arrays
features.reason: Current palette/light parsing defaults or defers malformed data while official PalettedContainer/SerializableChunkData codecs are bounded; state-id/property parity is not proven for every generated state.
features.expected: Official codecs decode block_states and biomes through registry-aware PalettedContainer codecs, retain only sections inside the LevelHeightAccessor range, serialize section Y plus optional BlockLight/SkyLight, and read/write heightmap long arrays as modeled values. Codec failures are represented as decode failures rather than silently inventing missing packed words.
features.current: Pumpkin maps block compound palettes to BlockStateId and biome strings to u8, uses disk minimum bits of 4 for blocks and 0 for biomes, and writes the expected section keys. However short packed arrays are filled with zero/default values, out-of-range palette indices default instead of failing, unknown biome names map to biome 0, section Y/count is not strictly range-validated, heightmap arrays are accepted without the required 37-long shape check, and LightContainer::get assumes 1024 bytes although load accepts any byte-array length.
features.first_repro: Static input: section block_states with a palette index beyond palette.len(), packed data shorter than the required volume, or a BlockLight byte array shorter than 1024. Official PalettedContainer codec/SerializableChunkData path returns a codec/decode failure or a bounded DataLayer; current code defaults missing entries and retains malformed light data until a later indexed get.

features.name: DataVersion validation, chunk migrations, and DataFixTypes.CHUNK
features.reason: Current chunk read/write stamps WORLD_DATA_VERSION but has no chunk DataVersion validation or DataFixTypes.CHUNK update path; official DFU exposes that boundary.
features.expected: The official artifact exposes a CHUNK DataFixTypes reference with update/updateToCurrentVersion; chunk loading must apply the chunk DataFixer before current SerializableChunkData parsing, and current writes stamp the current data version.
features.current: Pumpkin validates DataVersion ranges for level.dat through world_info (4435..4903) and writes WORLD_DATA_VERSION=4903 into ChunkData and ChunkEntityData. ChunkData::internal_from_bytes never reads or validates the chunk DataVersion and there is no current DataFixer/DataFixTypes.CHUNK call in the chunk read path. An old or future chunk can therefore be parsed as current and rewritten as 4903 without migration evidence.
features.first_repro: Static input: chunk root DataVersion=4435 or a value above 4903 with otherwise valid xPos/zPos/sections. Official has a CHUNK DataFixTypes migration boundary; current ChunkData::internal_from_bytes accepts the root without checking and internal_to_bytes emits 4903.

features.name: corrupt versus missing region/chunk classification and propagation
features.reason: Missing slots are separated from malformed compression/NBT and io_read_work sends load failures rather than silently generating; remaining region-level salvage scope was not run.
features.expected: An absent slot/region is represented as no chunk stream. Official RegionFileStorage returns null for no stream and for some invalid stream-version boundaries, while malformed NBT/I/O can propagate as IOException; higher-level loading must not silently regenerate or overwrite data without an explicit policy.
features.current: A missing OS file or empty/default serializer yields Missing for an absent slot. An invalid region header, compression error, or NBT parse error is sent as LoadedData::Error. Current io_read_work requests one coordinate at a time, turns Missing into generation, and turns Error into terminal RecvChunk::LoadFailure; it no longer collapses corruption into a generated ProtoChunk. However AnvilChunkFile::read can fail the entire serializer for one out-of-bounds entry, and invalid/malformed entry salvage is not per-slot equivalent.
features.first_repro: Static input: one requested slot has no location entry versus one has a legal location with unsupported compression or malformed NBT. Current paths produce Missing for the first and terminal LoadFailure for the second; a malformed region entry outside file bounds still aborts serializer creation for the region.

limitations: No fixture, server, or scheduler execution was run.

features.name: LinearV2/Pump alternative storage versus vanilla Anvil interoperability
features.reason: LinearV2/Pump are explicit custom formats outside the vanilla Anvil target.
features.expected: Only Anvil .mca plus official region compression/external-chunk conventions are a vanilla world interoperability target. A custom backend may intentionally optimize Pumpkin-only storage, but it must not be reported as a vanilla match unless conversion/interoperability is explicitly promised.
features.current: LinearV2 uses a custom signature/superblock, bitmap, bucket metadata, zstd compression, xxhash, footer signature, and .linear files. Pump uses an unnamed NBT envelope with region coordinates, per-chunk zstd-compressed byte arrays, and .pump files. Neither is readable by official RegionFileStorage; both are explicit configuration alternatives and are therefore outside the vanilla-compatible storage target.
features.first_repro: Static input: select ChunkConfig::Linear or ChunkConfig::Pump and write a region. The output extension/signature/container is not an official r.<x>.<z>.mca RegionFile stream; vanilla RegionFileStorage has no decoder for either format.

A custom backend may intentionally optimize Pumpkin-only storage, but it must not be reported as a vanilla match unless conversion/interoperability is explicitly promised.
raw_record.current: LinearV2 uses a custom signature/superblock, bitmap, bucket metadata, zstd compression, xxhash, footer signature, and .linear files. Pump uses an unnamed NBT envelope with region coordinates, per-chunk zstd-compressed byte arrays, and .pump files. Neither is readable by official RegionFileStorage; both are explicit configuration alternatives and are therefore outside the vanilla-compatible storage target.

limitations: This exclusion does not assess custom-format performance or Pumpkin-to-Pumpkin correctness beyond source/tests inventory.
No migration/conversion tool was found or evaluated.

features.name: gameTime/dayTime advancement, fixed-time dimensions, moon phase/angle, clock rate/pause and network time
features.reason: The finding is not 'worldtime.tick moves, therefore fixed-time is wrong'. Current Pumpkin does carry has_fixed_time=true for Nether/End, and EnvironmentAttributes uses that flag to suppress several day-dependent gameplay samples. The actual residual root is clock ownership and visual time: LevelTime::tick increments world_age for every World and advances time_of_day for every World when advance_time is enabled; each World owns a separate LevelTime, while world_clocks persistence reads/writes only minecraft:overworld. Official DimensionType separately exposes hasFixedTime and Optional defaultClock; the 26.2 Nether resource is fixed with no default_clock, while End is fixed with default_clock minecraft:the_end. Official MinecraftServer::createLevels constructs non-overworld levels with DerivedLevelData and ServerLevel's tickTime constructor flag false, so non-overworld gameTime/dayTime ownership is derived/shared rather than independent per-dimension clocks. The current code therefore has a real shared-owner/defaultClock/visual-solar boundary, but a moving gameTime/dayTime tick alone is not sufficient proof of mismatch.
features.expected: Official ServerLevel invalidates environment cache, uses SleepStatus/defaultClock wake markers, advances game time through tickTime, and treats fixed-time dimensions as not bright/dark-cycle dimensions. Moon brightness/phase and clock behavior derive from the dimension clock/timeline rather than an always-running universal day clock.
features.current: Pumpkin has world_age/time_of_day, rate and paused controls, network CUpdateTime/CSetTime, moon-phase timeline sampling and time commands. World::tick_environment advances every World::level_time and computes night from time_of_day; Dimension::has_fixed_time is used by some environment samples but LevelTime itself is not held at the official fixed clock/defaultClock contract. world_clocks persistence is effectively overworld-only in AnvilLevelInfo.
features.impact: Current Nether/End can have independently advancing LevelTime state and their visual sun/moon angle functions directly sample that local time_of_day. This can affect /time query/set semantics, day/night-derived environment sampling, sleep wake behavior, and reload ownership. The current has_fixed_time gates are a partial match and prevent a blanket claim that every visual/gameplay result is wrong; official fixed/default clock and shared gameTime/dayTime ownership are not represented.
features.first_repro: Static path: create the configured Overworld/Nether/End Worlds -> each World::load initializes its own LevelTime::new -> each World::tick_environment calls LevelTime::tick(advance_time) -> environment.rs VisualSunAngle/VisualMoonAngle use local get_time_of_day, while anvil world_clocks persistence only applies minecraft:overworld. Compare with official createLevels: overworld ServerLevel plus non-overworld DerivedLevelData and fixed/default clock resources. No runtime trace was run.

features.name: rain/thunder state, transition levels, cycle gamerule, weather persistence and weather client events
features.reason: Weather::tick_weather calls advance_weather_cycle only when !weather_cycle_enabled, although Weather::new initializes that field true. World::tick_environment also does not pass GameRuleRegistry.advance_weather into this gate. The current transition/event fields exist, but the default live cycle branch is statically inverted relative to the official ServerLevel::advanceWeatherCycle/ADVANCE_WEATHER contract. Weather default values and an administrator choosing advance_weather=false are policy/default distinctions, not separate findings.
features.expected: WeatherData stores clear/rain/thunder timers and booleans. ServerLevel advances weather only under the live tick/gamerule path, maintains old/current rain and thunder levels, and sends the official begin/end/rain-level/thunder-level client effects. Missing/corrupt saved data follows official saved-data codec/default boundaries.
features.current: Pumpkin stores the five weather fields and sends CGameEvent transitions/levels. Weather::tick_weather contains the cycle transition logic, but its condition is `if !weather_cycle_enabled { advance_weather_cycle(); }`, and World::tick_environment does not read GameRuleRegistry.advance_weather before ticking. read_weather/write_weather fall back to defaults on errors and add a custom DataVersion wrapper; only clear_weather_time is copied into LevelData during world-info load.
features.first_repro: Static input: Weather::new() -> tick_weather(). The cycle branch is skipped at the default true value; a separate `advance_weather=false` rule mutation is not routed into the same gate. No build/test/server run.

features.name: SleepStatus active/sleeping counts, players_sleeping_percentage, deep-sleep check, wake-up time and weather reset
features.reason: The raw report overstates absence: World::should_skip_night implements ceil(active_count*percentage/100) with a minimum of one and Player::sleeping_since is advanced to a deep-sleep threshold. It is nevertheless not an official SleepStatus equivalent: player_count includes spectators, the count is recomputed from a Player-owned sleeping_since field rather than separate active/sleeping status, and BedBlock still has a villager-wake TODO. The exact spectator predicate and deep-sleep owner are statically different; the wake/weather transition and multiplayer result were not executed.
features.expected: Official excludes spectators, counts active/sleeping players, computes ceil(active*percentage/100) with minimum one, separately checks deep sleeping, advances the dimension default clock to wake marker, wakes all players, and resets weather only when ADVANCE_WEATHER and rain conditions permit.
features.current: Pumpkin tracks sleeping_since per Player and wakes players when should_skip_night() reports enough sleep, but no SleepStatus owner/update/count/deep-sleep implementation was found. BedBlock uses a hard-coded monster ID list and calls Player::sleep; World::tick_environment handles wake/weather reset through local predicates. Bed occupancy and villager wake-up are incomplete (`TODO: Wake up villager`).
features.first_repro: Static input: one spectator plus one active player, then compare current player_count/required_sleeping with SleepStatus.update. A two-player 50/100 percentage fixture and villager occupancy fixture were not run.

features.name: border center/size transition, clamp/containment, damage/safe zone, warning state, persisted settings and client packets
features.reason: Current Worldborder has center/diameter/lerp/warning helpers and LevelData stores border fields, but World::load constructs a fresh default Worldborder without applying those persisted fields and World::tick has no Worldborder::tick call. The current new defaults also use warning_time=300 and damage_per_block=0.0, whereas official WorldBorder defaults are warningTime=15 and damagePerBlock=0.2; reset uses 29,999,984 as the diameter instead of the official 59,999,968 static size. These are concrete state-owner/default differences, not terrain-dependent claims.
features.expected: Official border is SavedData with center, static/moving extent, lerp duration/target/speed, absolute max size, safe zone, damage per block, warning blocks/time; ServerLevel ticks the moving extent every normal tick, applies settings, and listener/client state follows each mutation.
features.current: Pumpkin has center/old/new diameter, speed, portal boundary, warnings, damage and buffer fields plus Java initialization/set/lerp packets and contains/clamp helpers. World::tick does not call Worldborder::tick, World::load constructs a default border without copying LevelData border fields, and entity border damage/collision/warning side effects were not found in the shared world tick. LevelData read/write does preserve most NBT settings.
features.first_repro: Static input: saved border_size_lerp_time>0 or a border lerp followed by one World::tick; official extent updates through WorldBorder.tick, while current World::tick has no border tick. Save/reload was not executed.

features.name: level.dat spawn/difficulty/commands/version, data/minecraft saved-data ownership, dimension storage and fallback behavior
features.reason: Pumpkin has current data-version bounds, level.dat fields, world_gen_settings/game_rules/weather/clock companion files, and fallback parsing. Official LevelStorageSource injects registry context, reads typed SavedData codecs, bakes registry-backed WorldDimensions/LevelStem, and PrimaryLevelData persists RespawnData/game time/difficulty settings/data configuration. Current LevelData stores one spawn/difficulty owner and World::load selects a fixed Dimension enum, so per-dimension/custom registry ownership and exact corrupt-file semantics remain partial. Nether/End/worldgen gaps are not counted again as separate severity rows.
features.expected: Official loads level data plus registry-backed WorldGenSettings/dimensions, validates/fixes data versions, preserves respawn data, game time, difficulty lock, world settings and data configuration, and stores dimension-specific data under official level/dimension paths.
features.current: Pumpkin reads/writes level.dat and companion data files, has explicit data-version checks, backup/level.dat_new replacement, spawn/difficulty/version fields and world-gen settings parsing. However `LevelData.spawn` is effectively overworld-only, companion clocks/weather are not fully per-dimension owners, and dimension resolution is a fixed/generated Dimension enum rather than LevelStorageSource registry-baked LevelStem fallback. Read errors can fall back to defaults in companion files while level.dat is treated more strictly.
features.first_repro: Static input: load a level with custom dimension registry data and corrupt companion data, then compare registry/path/fallback ownership. No filesystem fixture was run.

features.name: world spawn location/rotation, spawn protection input, forced chunk persistence/loading/simulation and /forceload ownership
features.reason: Current /forceload does mutate ActiveChunkTracker.forced_chunks and update_active_chunks, so the raw wording 'no forced implementation' is too broad. The remaining difference is concrete: the set is in-memory World state, is not persisted as official FORCED tickets, and the command does not call the existing ChunkLoading::add_force_ticket/remove_force_ticket API. Official FORCED tickets carry persistent loading/simulation/keep-dimension-active semantics. Spawn position/protection is a separate policy/state boundary and is not severity-added here.
features.expected: Official world spawn is respawn data with dimension/position/yaw/pitch; forced chunks use persistent FORCED tickets that keep loading, ticking/simulation and dimension active, independent of nearby players. Spectator generation and spawn protection are separate policies.
features.current: Pumpkin reads spawn_x/y/z/yaw/pitch and uses them for spawn/protection; level.dat serialization hardcodes spawn compound dimension minecraft:overworld. ActiveChunkTracker has an in-memory forced_chunks set and the command changes that set, but repository grep found no command caller of ChunkLoading::add_force_ticket/remove_force_ticket. Therefore forced positions affect the active snapshot when present but do not establish official persistent loading/keep-dimension-active ticket ownership.
features.first_repro: Static input: /forceload add on an unloaded chunk with no nearby player, then restart/evict. Current in-memory forced membership exists until process/world owner reset; official FORCED ticket persistence and simulation ownership were not runtime-tested.

features.name: NetherPortalBlock axis/shape invalidation, portal collision entry, transition delay, piglin spawning and gamerule/environment gating
features.reason: Current axis-aware invalidation, portal collision, player/non-player delay lookup, cooldown processing and random zombified-piglin route cover substantial subcontracts. Exact official predicates are not complete: official entityInside first uses Entity.canUsePortal and the portal state; current collision directly calls try_use_portal, which gates configured dimension availability but no consumer of GameRuleRegistry.allow_entering_nether_using_portals was found. Official piglin spawning uses isSpawningMonsters, environment attribute, anyPlayerCloseEnoughForSpawning and BlockState.isValidSpawn; current uses spawn_mobs/difficulty, get_closest_player(128) and side-solid checks. Shape/client local transition/animation parity is also not established.
features.expected: Official validates portal shape on neighbor changes, marks entities inside a portal only when canUsePortal, computes player transition time from creative/default delay with max(0), uses PortalForcer destination logic, and gates piglin spawning by monster spawning, difficulty, environment attribute and nearby-player/spawn predicates.
features.current: Pumpkin has axis-aware neighbor validation, collision-to-target-world, player/non-player delay lookup, portal cooldown processing and random Zombified Piglin spawning. It uses a fixed portal cooldown/Entity.try_use_portal path, a hard-coded player lookup and local spawn checks; ALLOW_ENTERING_NETHER_USING_PORTALS is present in GameRules but no consumer was found in this block path. Portal block behavior also does not expose the official local transition/collision shape/client animation contract.
features.first_repro: Static input: collide with a Nether portal while allow_entering_nether_using_portals=false, or compare a portal-base block that is side-solid but not isValidSpawn. No runtime toggle/spawn fixture was run.

features.name: dimension coordinate scale, destination clamp, relative portal position, collision-free exit, yaw rotation and portal cooldown/transition completion
features.reason: The coordinate-scale ratio and 0/80 player delay values are represented, but exact predicates and ownership differ. Current Entity::try_use_portal checks portal_cooldown and resets it to the default when nonzero, while official canUsePortal/setAsInsidePortal/setPortalCooldown owns the transition state; current transition also does not consume allow_entering_nether_using_portals. Current scale handling floors/clamps to a block before search and uses a custom 1-block collision scan; official clamps a Vec3 and uses PortalShape.findCollisionFreePosition. The cooldown/gamerule predicate differences are static; final terrain-dependent position/collision results are unknown without runtime.
features.expected: Official uses current/destination coordinateScale ratio, clamps target X/Z to destination WorldBorder, preserves relative position in the full portal rectangle, finds collision-free output, rotates relative to axes and applies the Entity portal cooldown/transition state. features.current: Pumpkin computes current/destination coordinate_scale, clamps X/Z with Worldborder::clamp_block, preserves a custom relative offset, searches a small collision-free area and rotates yaw by axis. End entry uses a fixed platform at (100,49/50,0), and leaving End uses LevelData spawn.

features.name: redstone_experiments feature flag selection and ExperimentalRedstoneWireEvaluator path
features.reason: Pumpkin resolves and reports minecraft:redstone_experiments, but no current caller selects an experimental wire evaluator. Official RedStoneWireBlock::useExperimentalEvaluator checks Level.enabledFeatures for FeatureFlags.REDSTONE_EXPERIMENTS; when true it constructs ExperimentalRedstoneWireEvaluator and uses orientation-aware queued turn-off/turn-on processing, otherwise it uses the default evaluator. Current redstone_wire::update_power_strength always executes one immediate default-like calculation, and its only behavior callers are RedstoneWireBlock::placed and on_neighbor_update. features.name: block-event ordering relative to scheduled block ticks, fluid ticks, and block entities
features.reason: World::tick flushes synced block events before tick_chunks; official ServerLevel::tick runs block/fluid ticks before runBlockEvents.
features.expected: Official ServerLevel ticks block/fluid scheduled ticks, chunk source, then runs block events, then entities and block entities; scheduled ticks use trigger time, priority, and subTickOrder with deduplication.
features.current: World::tick calls flush_synced_block_events before update_active_chunks and tick_chunks. tick_chunks then dispatches scheduled block ticks and fluid ticks; block entities tick later. Thus Pumpkin piston block events run before same-world scheduled ticks, while official runBlockEvents is after block/fluid ticks. Pumpkin's synced event queue is a Vec FIFO with no official triggerTick/priority/subTickOrder structure.
features.first_repro: Queue a piston block event and a scheduled repeater/observer tick for the same game tick. Official scheduled ticks execute before runBlockEvents; Pumpkin flushes synced block events at the start of World::tick. No trace was run.

features.name: signed saved delays and long trigger-tick horizon
features.reason: Signed saved delays and long internal deadlines are present; remaining boundary is public u8 scheduling and i32 persistence narrowing, not missing signed-delay support.
features.expected: Runtime triggerTick is long; persisted delay is signed int and is reconstructed relative to the current long game time. Negative saved delays are overdue, not invalid by type alone.
features.current: Pumpkin stores delay as i32 and deadline as i64, and accepts negative NBT delays. However the public scheduling APIs accept u8, limiting new scheduled delays to 0..255, and persistence narrows deadline-offset back to i32. The 256-slot ring is a wheel, not an official semantic maximum, but the API width and signed narrowing are real boundaries.

features.name: ClientIntention protocol version, hostname, port, and next-state field decoding
features.reason: Current hostname bound is 32767 for proxy forwarding versus official readUtf(255), while protocol/port/intent decoding is present. This is an intentional compatibility policy boundary, not a security conclusion.

features.name: Status versus login/transfer routing and protocol-version mismatch policy
features.reason: The official 26.2 ServerHandshakePacketListenerImpl::beginLogin requires protocol 776, but that is not the applicable Pumpkin contract for this path. Current Pumpkin explicitly models JavaMinecraftVersion::V_26_1=775 and V_26_2=776 in pumpkin-util/src/version.rs, maps 775 through from_protocol, generates per-version packet IDs, and declares LOWEST_SUPPORTED_MC_VERSION separately from CURRENT_MC_VERSION. PendingConnection::handle_handshake therefore performs an intentional supported-range gate rather than an accidental 26.2-only gate. Status still bypasses login version rejection as in the official route; transfer-disabled is checked before the version range. The raw 775-versus-776 difference is a Java-26.2-only comparison false positive and is withdrawn from the top defect list.
features.expected: Status routes to status protocols without login version rejection. Login accepts only the current official protocol 776; transfer is separately gated by acceptsTransfers. A non-current login protocol is disconnected with the official incompatibility/outdated path.
features.current: Status also bypasses version rejection. Login/transfer reject only below LOWEST_SUPPORTED or above CURRENT, so known older versions such as 775 are allowed into login instead of being rejected as non-current. Transfer-disabled is checked first. State is stored before the mismatch kick.
features.impact: Only a product requirement that forbids all older supported Java clients and requires current-protocol-only login would make 775 acceptance a defect. The inspected code and generated multi-version packet tables instead document compatibility with multiple versions.
features.first_repro: Static handshake input: login intention with protocol 775. Official 26.2 beginLogin takes the non-current incompatibility branch. Pumpkin maps 775 to V_26_1, retains the version, and does not kick because 775 is between LOWEST_SUPPORTED_MC_VERSION=1.7.2/protocol 4 and CURRENT_MC_VERSION=26.2/protocol 776. This is the intended extension; no login exchange or runtime reaction was measured.

limits.limitations: This is a static routing comparison; no login packet exchange or client-visible disconnect text was run.
limits.unconfirmed: No login packet exchange, client response, or runtime compatibility matrix was run.
limits.impact_conditions: Only a product requirement that forbids all older supported Java clients and requires current-protocol-only login would make 775 acceptance a defect. The inspected code and generated multi-version packet tables instead document compatibility with multiple versions.

features.name: Handshake trailing payload consumption
features.reason: Official PacketDecoder rejects readable handshake trailing bytes; current handshake handler routes after SHandShake::read without a generic empty-body check. This is a concrete malformed-packet handling difference.
features.expected: After the handshake codec reads all fields, PacketDecoder requires readableBytes()==0; extra bytes cause IOException and the connection is closed.
features.current: The handshake handler parses SHandShake but never calls require_empty_body on the remaining payload. A frame containing valid handshake fields plus extra bytes can transition state instead of being rejected at this handler boundary.
features.first_repro: Valid intention packet body followed by one arbitrary byte: official PacketDecoder sees readableBytes()>0 and throws; Pumpkin handle_handshake_packet leaves payload unexamined and calls handle_handshake. No runtime/test command was run.

limits.limitations: The current raw decoder's frame boundary and subsequent packet lifecycle were not executed. This is distinct from the recent status trailing-payload fix, which is present at HEAD and is not reissued here.

features.name: Player count and sample semantics
features.reason: Current count/sample cap exists, but insertion-order/no-anonymization differs from official random window/listing policy. Client privacy/list behavior was not runtime-tested.
features.expected: Online/max counts are reported; sample is capped at 12. Official selects a random contiguous window, shuffles it, and substitutes the anonymous profile for players that disallow listing. The status codec uses id and name fields.
features.current: Online is maintained in CachedStatus on add/remove. Sample is capped at 12 but is the first 12 entries in insertion order, never shuffled, and always exposes each stored UUID/name. features.name: Description, favicon, and secure-chat status fields
features.reason: Current secure-chat status key and favicon validation differ from official codec/resource handling. This is JSON/metadata compatibility; metadata alone is not a disconnect/security proof.
features.expected: ClientboundStatusResponsePacket wraps ServerStatus.CODEC in lenientJson(32767). Description is a lenient optional chat component, favicon is an optional data:image/png;base64 string loaded from a valid 64x64 PNG, and the JSON key is enforcesSecureChat with the server's enforceSecureProfile value (codec default false).
features.current: CStatusResponse writes the JSON string through write_string (the 32767-character bound), so the outer length contract is aligned. Description is always present as Pumpkin TextComponent JSON and is modified through ServerListPingEvent. Favicon uses data:image/png;base64 and 64x64 header checks for files at least 24 bytes long, but short/malformed bytes can pass and invalid configured files fall back to the bundled icon. Secure chat is always true but serializes as enforceSecureChat (singular), not the official enforcesSecureChat key (plural).
features.first_repro: Serialize the normal status response: official codec field is enforcesSecureChat; Pumpkin serde rename_all produces enforceSecureChat. features.name: dirty transition, concurrent mutation, and serialization snapshot boundary
features.reason: Separate is_dirty/load then mark_dirty(false) and live Arc serialization remain static risks; existing dirty rollback is not missing.
features.expected: A save selects an unsaved chunk, takes a serialization snapshot, and preserves a later mutation as unsaved for the next save. The official save path calls tryMarkSaved before SerializableChunkData.copyOf and routes the serialized snapshot to I/O.
features.current: Pumpkin reads is_dirty and then unconditionally mark_dirty(false) as two separate Relaxed atomic operations before update_chunk. A mutation between those operations can set dirty=true and then be cleared by the saver. update_chunk serializes the live Arc<ChunkData> asynchronously rather than an immutable snapshot; mutations during serialization can therefore mix with the bytes while the dirty bit only records a later retry.
features.impact: A mutation concurrent with a save can be absent from the written bytes and can lose its dirty transition, so a later save is not guaranteed to retry it.
features.first_repro: Synthetic only, not run: arrange a mutation between file_manager.rs:387 is_dirty and :388 mark_dirty(false), then reload the region and compare the mutation with the final dirty flag.

features.name: serialization/update error retryability
features.reason: save_chunks restores dirty on update failure; remaining gap is queued worker error propagation/retry ownership, especially after unload.
features.expected: An update/serialization failure must be surfaced and must not be treated as a successful clean save. Official IOWorker completes the returned future exceptionally when RegionFileStorage.write throws.
features.current: ChunkFileManager re-marks every chunk already cleared in the current batch when update_chunk fails and returns ChunkWritingError. The queue worker logs the error and releases its I/O lock, but does not retain/requeue the failed batch. Thus the direct serializer path is retryable, while the scheduler queue has no automatic retry policy.
features.impact: A serialization failure during an unload/queued save can be logged without a retry; a still-resident dirty chunk may be retried by a later sweep, but an unloaded holder is no longer available to do so.
features.first_repro: Synthetic only, not run: force AnvilChunkData::from_chunk to return an error from an io_write batch after the schedule has removed an unloaded holder; observe that io_write_work logs and releases without resubmitting the chunk.

limitations: No failure-injection run was permitted.
Official exception propagation is static; vanilla retry policy beyond the returned future was not inferred.

features.name: region flush/write error and retry after partial save
features.reason: Region-write failure restores dirty in the file manager; remaining gap is queued retry ownership, not the old dirtyrollback defect.
features.expected: A flush/write failure must be observable and must not erase the only in-memory indication that the chunk still needs persistence. Explicit synchronization must wait for the queued storage operation.
features.current: ChunkFileManager re-marks cleared chunks when serializer.write fails and returns an error. But io_write_work only logs Failed to save chunks, decrements the lock, and continues; it does not retry or propagate the error to World::save/Server::save_all. If the chunk was removed during unload, the retryable Arc is no longer owned by the scheduler. The file-manager barrier only waits for operations already running, not failed queue ownership.

features.name: manual save completion acknowledgement versus durable chunk persistence
features.reason: The prior ack claim must be narrowed to the vanilla distinction between save-all and save-all flush. Official SaveAllCommand maps plain /save-all to saveEverything(true,false,true) and /save-all flush to saveEverything(true,true,true). Plain save-all intentionally schedules background I/O: MinecraftServer::saveAllChunks with flush=false uses ServerLevel::save(..., false, ...), SavedDataStorage::scheduleSave, and does not join chunk I/O. Flush mode calls SavedDataStorage::saveAndJoin and ChunkMap::saveAllChunks(true), which calls IOWorker.synchronize(true).join. Pumpkin routes both command forms to the same SaveAllExecutor, Server::save_all has no flush parameter, and World::save only sets should_save and notifies GenerationSchedule; it never provides the flush-mode wait/error result. Therefore an acknowledgement before all background bytes finish is not by itself a defect for plain save-all, but the explicit flush contract is missing.
features.expected: The manual save acknowledgement should follow the requested world/player save contract; official full save calls PlayerList.saveAll, saves levels, and in flush mode joins SavedData/ChunkMap I/O synchronization before returning.
features.current: The command spawns Server::save_all and sends success after it returns. World::save only sets should_save and notifies the schedule; it does not await the schedule's io_write queue, ChunkFileManager save_chunks, or a durable flush. Therefore success can be sent before chunk bytes are written and before a queued error is surfaced.
features.impact: Plain /save-all is not reclassified as wrong merely because the background I/O worker may still be draining after the success boundary. The real residual difference is /save-all flush: Pumpkin acknowledges through the same non-flush path, so a caller cannot rely on the requested durable synchronization or a propagated queued-write error. Shutdown and process-failure windows can therefore pass the flush command boundary without the vanilla flush guarantee.
features.first_repro: Static path: invoke /save-all and /save-all flush -> both select SaveAllExecutor -> Server::save_all -> World::save -> should_save=true + level_channel.notify -> GenerationSchedule::work later enters save_all_chunk and io_write_work. There is no flush boolean, wait future, IOWorker-like synchronize, or error result in the flush branch. No runtime delay/failure fixture was run.
existing_tests: No current test found that waits for save-all acknowledgement and then verifies chunk persistence (read-only search).

features.name: save-off/save-on, autosave suppression, and save-all flush semantics
features.reason: save-off gates autosave while manual save still requests a save; remaining difference is the non-durable shared flush path.
features.expected: save-off disables ordinary/autosave writes while a forced/manual save remains distinguishable; save-on restores ordinary saves. A flush/manual variant must await its storage synchronization contract.
features.current: save-off/on toggles Level.save_enabled, and only the autosave branch checks it. Server::save_all does not check save_enabled, so manual save still requests saves, which is a useful match to forced-save intent. However the `flush` command is the same executor as save-all and inherits the missing queue/flush wait; the toggle has no durable-save barrier or pending-write state.
features.impact: The toggle itself controls autosave, but `/save-all flush` can acknowledge before the flush is complete, making the command mode misleading during shutdown/failure windows.

features.name: player disconnect, world save, chunk worker drain, and world-info shutdown ordering
features.reason: Shutdown timeout warns while queued IO/cancellation/completion is not one durable result.
features.expected: Shutdown stops intake, saves players, drains/synchronizes world I/O, closes levels/storage, and only then closes the level-storage access. Official stopServer explicitly saves players, performs saveAllChunks, closes each ServerLevel, SavedDataStorage, and LevelStorageAccess.

features.name: unload save ownership and queued worker drain
features.reason: Terrain unload removes holder ownership before queued write completion; worker failure logs/releases without restore or requeue.
features.expected: Unloading a chunk must retain save ownership until the storage future completes; shutdown/manual save must drain unload work before storage close.
features.current: process_unload_queue removes the holder and only then sends dirty Level/eligible Proto chunks to the bounded io_write queue. The worker decrements the per-position I/O lock after either success or failure, and failure is only logged. Entity clean-up has an explicit restore-on-error path, but the terrain unload queue has no equivalent reinsert/retry path.
features.impact: An unload-time write failure can leave no loaded holder and no queued retry, so the concrete loss window is the failed write after holder removal.
features.first_repro: Synthetic only, not run: queue one dirty unload chunk, fail its write, then inspect chunk_map, io_lock, and the next unload/autosave sweep for a requeue.

features.name: worker queue backpressure, timeout, cancellation, and bounded shutdown
features.reason: Queue capacity 500 plus blocking_send and cancellation-blind IO lacks a bounded completion contract comparable to official synchronize/close.
features.expected: Backpressure should be bounded and shutdown should have an explicit completion/cancellation policy that does not silently abandon queued writes.
features.current: Pumpkin uses a Tokio mpsc queue of capacity 500 and calls blocking_send from the scheduler. The I/O worker explicitly ignores cancellation while saving. Level::shutdown gives scheduler thread joining a 3-second timeout, but the blocked sender has no per-save timeout or cancellation branch; it can delay shutdown beyond that warning boundary. Official ChunkMap limits active writes at 128 and IOWorker exposes synchronize/close futures for ordered drain.
features.impact: A saturated or stalled storage worker can block the scheduler and make shutdown unbounded from the caller's perspective, while the advertised timeout does not cancel the underlying queue operation.
features.first_repro: Synthetic only, not run: fill the 500-entry write queue with a worker that never completes; invoke Level::shutdown and compare timeout return with actual io_write task termination.
existing_tests: No current blocked-save/backpressure cancellation test found (read-only search).

limitations: No queue stress or shutdown run.
The official active-write value 128 is a static bytecode constant, not a Pumpkin throughput target.

limits.open_questions: Whether the outer runtime force-exits after the task wait is outside this static audit.

features.name: atomic replace, fsync/force, and backup behavior for level/body files
features.reason: Formats mix direct/in-place writes and flush/rename without a common force/sync and backup contract; crash outcome was not executed.
features.expected: Metadata save uses a temp file plus safe replacement and old backup. Region storage uses a FileChannel and explicit force/sync mode; flush means the bytes are forced according to the storage contract.
features.current: Pumpkin level.dat uses level.dat_new, copies the prior file to level.dat_old, then renames; it does not call File::sync_all. The data/minecraft/*.dat writers use File::create directly. Linear/Anvil full rewrites flush then rename without sync; Anvil in-place writes flush the existing file directly; Pump writes directly with tokio::fs::write. Thus atomicity varies by format and durable fsync/backup is not a shared contract.
features.impact: A process or OS crash during direct/in-place writes can leave a partial body or metadata file; lack of forced durability also leaves a post-success crash window even when rename is atomic.
features.first_repro: Synthetic only, not run: interrupt each writer between flush/rename or during direct write, then compare surviving old/new/body files and reload classification.

limitations: No crash or power-loss simulation.
This finding is about concrete write mechanics, not a metadata/body semantic difference alone.
limits.unconfirmed: No build/test/server/client/runtime command was run; runtime_verified=false
limits.open_questions: Platform-specific rename replacement and filesystem durability need an isolated fixture; the real world directory was not touched.

features.name: player data, world metadata, chunks, entities, and world-info save ordering
features.reason: Manual order is world-info then player/advancement then World::save, unlike official PlayerList.saveAll then saveAllChunks; consistency ordering, not automatic loss.
features.expected: Official saveEverything first calls PlayerList.saveAll, then saveAllChunks. saveAllChunks saves per-level data, chunk storage, and entity persistence; the stop path also saves players before worlds.
features.current: Pumpkin Server::save_all writes world metadata first, then online player data, then advancements, then each World::save. World::save writes live entities/block entities/POI/custom data and only queues terrain chunks. Graceful process shutdown separately saves player data/advancements before Server::shutdown, so shutdown order differs from manual save-all order.
features.impact: The ordering creates a mixed-generation snapshot if a failure occurs between metadata/player/chunk stages; the concrete risk is consistency and recovery selection, not an automatic claim that every metadata/body mismatch loses terrain.

features.reason: Data-file errors and chunk queue completion are not represented by one durable save result; this is separate from dirty rollback.

features.name: Block.setBlock update-flag bitmask 1/2/4/16/32/64/512 and side-effect meanings
features.reason: Official mask is 1/2/4/8/16/32/64/128/256/512; Pumpkin local flags alias MOVED/UPDATE_KNOWN_SHAPE at 16. Qualified local contract boundary, not external exploit.
features.expected: Official flags are independent: 1 queues neighborChanged, 2 sends client updates subject to client/full-chunk conditions unless 4 suppresses them, 16 suppresses shape updates, 32 suppresses drops, 64 marks piston movement, 128 skips redstone-wire shape updates, 256 skips block-entity side effects, and 512 skips onPlace; the default Level.setBlock overload uses updateLimit=512.
features.current: Pumpkin defines 1/2/4/16/32/64/128 but maps 8 to SKIP_DROPS, aliases 16 as MOVED and UPDATE_KNOWN_SHAPE, maps 32 to redstone-wire suppression, 64 to the block-entity replacement callback, and 128 to the block-added callback. There is no 256 side-effect bit or 512 update-limit/on-place bit. Internal callers use Pumpkin's remapped names, so this is not an external API claim, but the official bitmask contract is not preserved.
features.first_repro: Not executed: compare flags 32, 64, 256, and 512 at Level.setBlock/LevelChunk.setBlockState. Official 32 is UPDATE_SUPPRESS_DROPS and 512 is UPDATE_SKIP_ON_PLACE; Pumpkin's same numeric values invoke different local meanings or have no named representation.

limits.limitations: Static only; no source/config/test edit, build, test, server/client, packet capture, or commit.

features.name: Neighbor notification versus neighbor-shape callbacks and their ordering/shape limit
features.reason: Neighbor callbacks/order exist, but official shape passes, flag masking, and updateLimit decrement are not the same bounded path. Static only.
features.expected: After the block is accepted, official setBlock performs bit-1 neighborChanged dispatch, then if bit 16 is clear and updateLimit > 0 performs indirect-neighbor-shape, direct-neighbor-shape, and indirect-neighbor-shape passes with flags masking clients/suppressed drops and limit-1. Shape traversal follows the official direction order.
features.current: Pumpkin dispatches update_neighbors_at for bit NOTIFY_NEIGHBORS, then, unless MOVED/UPDATE_KNOWN_SHAPE is present, invokes prepare(old), update_neighbors, and prepare(new). update_neighbors calls get_state_for_neighbor_update on each adjacent position, but there is no updateLimit argument and no explicit indirect/direct/indirect three-pass sequence. features.name: Block replacement callbacks, drops, block-entity side effects, and onPlace suppression
features.reason: Block-entity/on-place hooks exist, but official 256/512 side effects and fluid beforeDestroyingBlock/drop semantics are not mapped one-to-one; static only.
features.expected: Official LevelChunk removes/replaces block entities when the block type changes, runs preRemoveSideEffects unless bit 256 is set, runs affectNeighborsAfterRemoval according to neighbor/move flags, runs onPlace unless bit 512 is set, and fluid replacement invokes the fluid's beforeDestroyingBlock contract rather than an unconditional player-style break path. Drops are controlled by UPDATE_SUPPRESS_DROPS=32 and the specific replacement path.
features.current: World::set_block_state invokes the old entity's on_block_replaced unless SKIP_BLOCK_ENTITY_REPLACED_CALLBACK (local bit 64), removes live and pending entities, calls on_placed for the new block and on_placed_fluid for the resolved fluid, and uses break_block for explicit destruction/drops. Local bit 32 skips redstone-wire replacement and local bit 128 skips on_placed; there is no official 256/512 mapping. Fluid apply_spread calls break_block for non-air non-fluid targets, which can route through BlockBreakEvent/loot rather than the official fluid beforeDestroyingBlock contract.

features.name: Block light and sky light updates after block-state mutation
features.reason: Pumpkin propagates light synchronously; official queues checkBlock then runLightUpdates with section/sky lifecycle. Lifecycle difference only; static only.
features.expected: A changed block state is compared by light dampening, emission, and shape occlusion. features.name: official worldgen resource coverage, generated registries, and custom datapack worldgen loading
features.reason: Compile-time built-ins exist, but arbitrary runtime datapack worldgen codec/registry loading is absent; resource counts are not terrain proof.
features.expected: Official 26.2 resolves noise settings, density/noise parameters, surface rules, biome sources, structures, placed features, and processor/template resources through codecs/registries. A custom datapack resource can alter the worldgen graph without recompiling the server.
features.current: Pumpkin embeds generated Rust registries and compile-time datapack/template data. The standard generated breadth matches several counts (biome=66, configured_feature=226, placed_feature=262, structure=34, structure_set=20, template_pool=188), but the repo resource layout is not byte-identical to the selected inner JAR: official worldgen JSON count=963, repo assets worldgen file count=1032; official density_function=35 versus repo density_function=55; official configured_carver path=4 versus repo carver path=4 plus material_condition=8 and material_rule=41. Level loading accepts a small set of generator/biome-source shapes and fixed settings names; it does not resolve arbitrary custom noise settings, density functions, surface rules, biome parameter lists, structure sets, or placed features at runtime. Custom datapack worldgen is unsupported and must not be inferred from matching registry counts.
features.first_repro: Static input: add a non-minecraft worldgen/noise_settings or density_function entry and reference it from world_gen_settings.dat. Current Level::from_root_folder only maps flat or a known settings reference into generated static tables; no runtime datapack registry/codec path is present. No runtime was run.

limits.limitations: Resource counts and selected resource hashes are inventory evidence only; they do not prove terrain equivalence. features.name: seed derivation, positional random factories, legacy random source selection, and Nether/End generator RNG
features.reason: Official RandomState selects LEGACY/XOROSHIRO from NoiseGeneratorSettings; current GlobalRandomConfig starts Xoroshiro even when legacy_random_source=true. Same-seed output was not run.
features.expected: RandomState selects WorldgenRandom.Algorithm.LEGACY or XOROSHIRO from NoiseGeneratorSettings, forks positional random factories, and derives named aquifer/ore streams from that selected source. Noise, aquifer, ore, carver, decoration, and structure seeds must use the correct source and seed-reset boundaries for the dimension.
features.current: GlobalRandomConfig::new always starts with Xoroshiro::from_seed(seed).next_splitter() even when legacy_random_source=true. The base DoublePerlinNoiseBuilder always calls NormalNoise::from_params(..., legacy=false); only two Nether shifted-noise ids and selected interpolated-noise paths special-case LegacyRand. NoiseSettings marks NETHER, END, CAVES, and FLOATING_ISLANDS legacy_random_source=true, so their ordinary noise/router/surface streams are not wired through the official legacy algorithm. Population/decorator and large-feature formulas themselves have focused tests, but that does not repair the dimension-wide source selection.
features.first_repro: Static input: seed=42, dimension=THE_NETHER or THE_END. Official RandomState receives a NoiseGeneratorSettings whose getRandomSource is LEGACY; current VanillaGenerator passes legacy_random_source=true into GlobalRandomConfig but still constructs the base splitter with Xoroshiro and builds ordinary noise with legacy=false. Same-seed generated blocks/biomes were not run, therefore output divergence remains runtime-unknown.

limits.limitations: Static call-path difference is established; no Cargo test, chunk generation, vanilla runtime, or same-seed output comparison was executed.
limits.unconfirmed: No build/test/server/client/worldgen/runtime command was run; runtime_verified=false

features.name: FeatureSorter-equivalent biome union, decoration-step order, feature index/seed, placement modifiers, and Nether/End ordering
features.reason: Non-Overworld feature selection assigns local sorted indices while official FeatureSorter/StepFeatureData and setFeatureSeed use dimension-wide ordering.
features.expected: Official decoration gathers possible biomes from the 3x3 neighborhood and uses FeatureSorter step/index data, resets the feature RNG with setFeatureSeed(populationSeed,index,step), then applies each placed feature/modifier in order with biome checking.
features.current: Pumpkin gathers distinct biome ids from the 3x3 cache, loops 11 steps, resets a WorldgenRandom from populationSeed + index + 10000*step, and implements many placement modifiers/features. Overworld uses a generated global order and has focused order tests. For a non-Overworld-only biome set, select_features sorts the selected features locally and assigns local indices; the source explicitly notes that Nether/End feature orders are not modeled. This can change both order and feature seed in Nether/End even though configured/placed feature counts match official counts (226/262).
features.first_repro: Static input: a Nether or End chunk whose 3x3 biome union contains only non-Overworld biomes. Current select_features uses local sorted/deduplicated indices; official FeatureSorter uses the dimension's global StepFeatureData. Same-seed feature block output was not run.

limits.limitations: No feature placement or same-seed chunk generation was run. Datapack custom placed/configured features are unsupported at runtime.

features.name: structure-set placement, random spread/concentric rings, exclusion/frequency, structure locate, and dimension-aware biome validation
features.reason: Structure locate uses the Overworld biome supplier for all dimensions; official locate state is dimension-aware.
features.expected: Placement state is built from the dimension's BiomeSource/RandomState and all structure sets; locate searches candidates and validates the requested structure using that same dimension-aware source, placement, exclusion, frequency, and generated-start rules.
features.current: RandomSpread, concentric rings, frequency methods, exclusion zones, and a stronghold cache are implemented. However find_nearest_structure_start hardcodes MultiNoiseBiomeSupplier::OVERWORLD when lazily validating every random-spread structure, even when the active world is Nether or End. A Nether /locate fortress or fossil path can therefore use the wrong biome source. The generic random-spread finder also breaks out of a radius after the first placement candidate instead of comparing all placement candidates in that radius; the command mostly passes one structure set at a time, but this is not the official all-candidate state contract.

features.name: structure piece generation order, jigsaw/template processors, block entities, deferred loot, and per-structure RNG
features.reason: Structure generation creates one step RNG with index 0 and reuses it; official resets feature seed per structure index.
features.expected: Each structure/structure start is placed in the official ordered step with its own feature seed; pieces, processors, jigsaw expansion, block-entity NBT, and deferred loot-table/loot-seed state see the same per-structure random stream and writable-area rules.
features.current: Pumpkin collects all structure collectors for a step, creates one random stream with get_decorator_seed(population_seed, 0, step), and passes that same mutable stream through every collector in task order. Official ChunkGenerator.applyBiomeDecoration resets setFeatureSeed(populationSeed, structureIndex, step) for each structure before placement. Therefore later structure pieces and processor AppendLoot seeds consume a different stream even if placement candidates match. Pumpkin has broad template/processor/jigsaw coverage and intentionally defers loot via LootTable/LootTableSeed NBT, but the per-structure RNG boundary is a confirmed static difference.
features.first_repro: Static input: one decoration step containing two structure starts and at least one processor AppendLoot/block-rotation draw. Official resets feature seed per structure index; current generate_structure_step seeds index=0 once and reuses the advanced stream. No structure runtime was run.
