features.name: flat layers/biome, flat decoration/lakes/structure overrides, debug-all-block-states, and generator-type dispatch
features.reason: Flat path lacks all FlatLevelGeneratorSettings feature/lake/structure override semantics and has no DebugLevelSource dispatch.
features.expected: Flat settings retain layers, biome, decoration/features, lakes, and structure overrides; debug_all_block_states dispatches to a distinct DebugLevelSource that fills the block-state grid rather than normal noise terrain.
features.current: FlatGenerator stores only seed, dimension, layers, and biome. Its noise stage fills layers and its surface/carver/features methods only advance the stage; parsed FlatPresetSettings.features/lakes are not carried into the generator and structure overrides are passed only to the noise generator branch. Level::from_root_folder dispatches only generator_type==minecraft:flat specially; debug_all_block_states is parsed as a world preset but no debug generator branch exists, so it falls through to ordinary noise generation.
features.first_repro: Static input: use minecraft:flat settings with features=true or lakes=true, then use debug_all_block_states preset. Current FlatGenerator does not run decoration/lakes/structures and Level::from_root_folder has no DebugLevelSource equivalent. No world was generated.

features.expected: A chunk stage has the required read/write neighborhood; missing required neighbors are not silently converted to air/no-op, cross-border structures/carvers/features are stable, and repeated/parallel generation with the same inputs produces the same normalized chunk state.
features.current: The generation cache is intentionally local and stage-dependent. Out-of-cache get_block_state logs and returns AIR, while set_block_state logs and no-ops. Structure generation scans up to radius 8 but skips absent neighbors; generate_single_chunk_with_radius uses only the stage direct radius (1 for Features/Full), while dedicated structure tests manually request radius 16. Structure starts are memoized through OnceLock/DashMap and local stage loops are serial, but no repeated parallel-vs-serial determinism check exists in this session. This is a boundary risk/unknown, not a claim that every normal scheduler path is nondeterministic.
features.first_repro: Generate a structure-bearing target twice with stage Features using direct radius=1 and explicit radius=16, then compare border blocks, references, pieces, and feature calls; repeat with serial and parallel scheduler workers. Not run.

features.name: selector priority, control conflict, interrupt, disable, and alternating tick cadence
features.reason: Exact only for shared GoalSelector arbitration and Mob tick parity, not every mob goal or runtime behavior.
features.expected: Running goals stop when disabled or canContinueToUse is false; a candidate must replace every conflicting control according to priority and canStop, then starts and ticks according to requiresUpdateEveryTick. Mob server AI alternates selector updates and running-goal ticks by tick/id parity.
features.current: Pumpkin keeps one running goal index per four Controls, checks disabled controls and should_continue, requires a strictly higher priority for replacement, honors can_stop, stops conflicting goals before start, and uses the same parity split in Mob::tick. features.impact: Shared selector arbitration and the observed official tick-order contract are represented for current Goal callers; runtime confirmation is still absent.

features.name: repath delay, path progress, stuck detection, timeout, and navigation stop
features.reason: Current and official 26.2 call paths were compared for the named condition. Current: `set_progress` always sets `path=None` and resets stuck timeout. Tempt, Breed, FollowParent, FollowOwner, and other goals call set_progress repeatedly, so `needs_new_path` sees no path and recomputes on the next tick despite `repath_cooldown=15`. Stuck detection and timeout fields exist, but their lifecycle is coupled to this path-clearing behavior. Expected: Existing paths are followed; recomputation is delayed/limited (official 20-tick recompute boundary); stuck detection can stop navigation without every progress request discarding the current path.
features.expected: Existing paths are followed; recomputation is delayed/limited (official 20-tick recompute boundary); stuck detection can stop navigation without every progress request discarding the current path.

features.name: use remainder conversion and use cooldown timing/group
features.reason: UseRemainderImpl is still a marker. Its NBT read ignores the input and default write_data returns End; the wire codec writes four zero VarInts and deserialize_item_stack_template decodes then discards the template. The nested ItemStack template helpers do exist in the current codec and are used by other components, but UseRemainder is not connected to one. UseCooldownImpl stores seconds/group and has a codec, but current callers start cooldown outside the official successful-use/finish owner: ItemRegistry::on_use, use_on_block, and use_on_entity start it unconditionally after their behavior call, while LivingEntity::tick starts it again when a consumable finishes. The Java and Bedrock entry paths both reach these callers; no separate current finish implementation was found.
features.expected: After a successful use, UseRemainder creates the configured ItemStackTemplate remainder and routes extra items to inventory/drop; UseCooldown applies positive seconds as ticks after use, using the configured group.
features.current: UseRemainderImpl is a marker: NBT read discards the template, NBT write emits no template fields, wire serialize emits four zero VarInts, and wire deserialize discards the decoded template. Cooldown data is stored, but ItemRegistry starts it for ordinary use/use-on-block/use-on-entity regardless of an explicit success result, and LivingEntity starts it again on finish.
features.impact: A configured use_remainder template is not preserved through the current component model/wire path and has no generic successful-use application path; only separate hardcoded potion/bottle handling exists in the finish path. Items with UseCooldown can receive an immediate cooldown even when use_on_block/use_on_entity returns Pass/Fail, and consumables can receive an immediate cooldown plus a second finish cooldown. Group naming is carried, but positive-seconds and identifier validation are weaker than the official codec.
features.first_repro: Static/runtime candidate: load an item with use_remainder={convert_into:{item:<item>,count:1,components:{...}}}; current NBT read produces marker state, current wire encode emits four zero VarInts, and decode discards the nested template. For cooldown, use a consumable with seconds=1 and a grouped cooldown: Java handle_use_item reaches ItemRegistry::on_use, then LivingEntity::tick reaches the finish block and starts the same group again; a use-on-block/item behavior returning Pass still reaches an unconditional start in ItemRegistry::use_on_block. No fixture was executed.

features.name: trajectory, gravity, drag, owner initialization, owner-collision release, and shared thrown-projectile tick
features.reason: Current and official 26.2 call paths were compared for the named condition. Current: Pumpkin stores only owner_id, skips the owner for the first five entity-age ticks, subtracts fixed gravity, applies 0.99 air or 0.8 water drag, moves with set_pos, then performs a custom swept AABB scan. Arrow/trident duplicate the movement path with family constants; fireballs apply acceleration before the shared scan. Owner references are not dynamic entity references and no owner-release/chunk-discard contract is present. Expected: Official projectiles retain an owner reference, dynamically determine when the projectile has left the owner collision range, apply per-family gravity/inertia, perform swept hit detection before final movement, update rotation/effects, and discard when the required owner/chunk state is unavailable.

features.name: hitboxes, block ray, entity hit ordering, collision filtering, and cancellable hit path
features.reason: Current and official 26.2 call paths were compared for the named condition. Current: Pumpkin expands both block and entity boxes by 0.3, scans block collision AABBs and entity AABBs, keeps the smallest t, skips owner for five ticks and most projectile types, and calls on_hit. The ProjectileHitEvent is created only by ArrowEntity::on_hit and its cancelled flag is not checked; other projectile families have no equivalent cancellable event. No official deflection/no-physics/entity selector contract is represented in the shared path. Expected: Block clipping and entity hit results are resolved along the movement vector, with official can-hit/no-physics/owner/projectile filters, nearest-hit ordering, deflection or hit callbacks, and the callback's cancellation semantics applied before side effects.

features.name: arrow piercing, critical hits, pickup modes, flame/punch, item state, and projectile-spawned enchantments
features.reason: Current and official 26.2 call paths were compared for the named condition. Current: ArrowEntity has critical, pickup, pierce, punch, flame, in-ground, item, weapon, and effect-color state; bow/crossbow creation applies damage, punch, piercing, intangible pickup, critical, and projectile-spawned enchantments. However pickup is not restored in read_custom_nbt, weapon/flame state is incomplete for persistence, and the pre-hit pierced_len/has_hit gate can prevent the subsequent pierce hit path before on_hit. Hit cancellation is ignored. Expected: Piercing permits the official number of entity hits while maintaining ignore/dead lists, critical damage and pickup modes are persisted and synced, weapon/projectile components are applied, and hit-side enchantment/post-hurt effects use the owner and damage source.

features.name: trident loyalty return, riptide launch, channeling, impaling, pickup, and ground lifecycle
features.reason: Current and official 26.2 call paths were compared for the named condition. Current: Pumpkin throws and grounds tridents, supports allowed/creative pickup, and implements a riptide branch when the player's current block is water. It applies a local impaling bonus only when the target is touching water. There is no loyalty return state/tick, no channeling/lightning path, no foil/loyalty tracked state, and no official trident damage-source/post-attack path. Expected: Loyalty tridents return to an acceptable live owner with no-physics movement, pickup/despawn rules depend on loyalty, riptide uses the official water/submersion conditions, channeling invokes lightning under the official weather/sky conditions, and trident damage/post-attack effects use trident sources and enchantment helpers.

features.name: item-use projectile generation parameters and both generation/tick caller paths
features.reason: Current and official 26.2 call paths were compared for the named condition. Current: handle_use_item validates packet yaw/pitch and forwards them to ItemRegistry::on_use_with_rotation, but the projectile ItemBehaviour implementations generally ignore the parameters and call player.rotation() instead. Stack propagation is inconsistent: eggs/potions copy stacks, arrows pass projectile/weapon stacks, but fireworks and XP bottles do not create stack-bearing projectile entities. Generation callers were traced through item use plus AI/mob callers; entity ticking has one current world caller `entity.tick(entity.as_ref(), server_ref)`, whose EntityBase dispatch reaches each projectile tick. No second independent projectile tick caller was found. Expected: The use-item packet's action yaw/pitch and held ItemStack/components reach projectile constructors; all spawned projectile entities enter the authoritative entity tick once through the world tick dispatcher, while AI/item callers use the same family constructors with explicit owner/stack/direction parameters.
features.expected: The use-item packet's action yaw/pitch and held ItemStack/components reach projectile constructors; all spawned projectile entities enter the authoritative entity tick once through the world tick dispatcher, while AI/item callers use the same family constructors with explicit owner/stack/direction parameters.

Generation callers were traced through item use plus AI/mob callers; entity ticking has one current world caller `entity.tick(entity.as_ref(), server_ref)`, whose EntityBase dispatch reaches each projectile tick. No second independent projectile tick caller was found.
features.impact: A client's packet rotation can be stale relative to the server's player rotation, causing thrown projectile direction differences; item components can be lost at generation, while the tick dispatch itself is centralized and statically complete.
features.first_repro: Static input: Use Item packet yaw/pitch differs from Player::rotation for an egg, snowball, pearl, potion, wind charge, or trident. handle_use_item passes the packet values to on_use_with_rotation, but those behaviours inherit the default method and then use player.rotation(). Static caller audit: `world/tick.rs:125` is the single entity tick call; `EntityBase::tick` dispatches to projectile-specific tick implementations.

limits.limitations: No packet/runtime generation or tick execution was run; AI spawn paths were statically enumerated only.
